Peter,
Today you will receive countless texts and emails from Democrats across the country reaching out for your support to help them close out their fundraising quarter as strongly as possible.
Unless the email is from Democrats in Virginia who are working to pass a ballot measure to redistrict in an April 21st special election, that fundraising message is not as important or as urgent as what we are sending you right now.
The fate of the '26 blue wave is in jeopardy because of MAGA's effort to rig the midterm election via red state redistricting. If we can't counter them via blue state redistricting, it won't matter how big the blue wave gets, the math won't work out for us, they win.
In Virginia, where Democrats have launched a last ditch ballot measure to create more blue congressional districts, Republicans now hold a lead in early voting and we are at risk of losing this April 21st race.

A MAGA dark-money group -- Advance Colorado, with deep ties to the far-right and even Russian oligarchs -- has introduced their own ballot initiative aimed at undercutting our efforts and gumming up the works to ensure MAGA keeps their seats.
If they succeed, CO Dems not only have to campaign for our redistricting initiative but we'll also have to campaign against theirs. This confuses the hell out of voters and kills our chances.
Our lawyers are fighting the MAGA ballot measure and are poised to force CO's Supreme Court to rule on the legality of it, however, if we lose our case (and we very well could), Democrats will not only have to run a Yes campaign for our effort and a No campaign against theirs - as such it will cost double if not double to run these concurrent efforts.

name: Kendra Brooks & Nicolas O'Rourke (via Working Families Party)
subject: Our latest congressional endorsement
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pennsylvania Working Families Party
body:
| | | Hey Peter, We’re **Kendra Brooks** and **Nicolas O’Rourke** — At-Large Philadelphia City Councilmembers elected on the Working Families Party ballot line. A few years ago, we proved what happens when working people organize and refuse to play by the rules written for us. We knocked off the Republicans and became Philly’s dominant minority party — not with big money, but with people power, block by block. That’s how we move. So when there’s a chance to send someone to Congress from our city, in a district that runs through West Philly, Center City, South Philly, and North Philly, we take it seriously. **That’s why we’re proud to share that the Working Families Party is endorsing Chris Rabb for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 3rd District.** [**If you’re ready to help send a real working-class champion from Philadelphia to Washington, split a contribution now between Chris Rabb’s campaign and WFP.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqt1KgGElNLHWwWbO_pXXNSCg46p33D0X80d2Llvy4PLrfymP_CJotGnz1e7mzvU409cyfPxpmXhe-jgHSDFLVs5oQ7MnAUxpTx44ExHjouIyob7aA_2COCD7WC7E9ZLNhHWauQhwUWdcrCE0iYFTcJTfvrr-w6IFA0euyXjsMRquCpPejyB1_rfvJIZsGXql1washFoeBme6uatdPE8-e0fwL-5373xBC2g85lOP1ZbW1QJf1k2HVKAtuGuAqtUSsIvPcp7MsxadUBRJrJXlbrbCTg4bAsGs-ZgPzakb7dsZxCUfpZ-_YMpOSn69nzTHQWUxN3RYC2tRa9DecqGLcoKaRj1FN8aThecORksowhuKzy_7AAmtylfBozdEPzApLh5K4Qb6VUtsr8vwfmgrkvt/4pe/uP3EnI-NQK2tTC0xqvcYjg/h0/h001.vn88ZRcBlr1IP8Fs_WZpLy-e75yNfctgmy8r4uWBz18) **[Donate $10 »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqt1KgGElNLHWwWbO_pXXNSCg46p33D0X80d2Llvy4PLrfymP_CJotGnz1e7mzvU40-VJt8rC6eJXGWJYq0s1Y1PCE8lQLFlsWk6ciY0I4lIS5Vra0AqdxSGHNYXqeMHhVKNLOcXzC0yHtmDTyj9waKVbbWyR9-d3lqLaBUMZ0eTLK3A7o5Nic2pEvLtpqurY3bumspEHoqN_o7CmzUktFkSK4YyVMC9vBe2AJc09fMtftZT1Je2r_9Dp5xwUzrz2puIfxhte_52RizgFR8x4BHYNX_ZStq_zrTqKs2uwCl9VPOItVx6VZVRknimMse6UIxtBj4c57GKlOr5dEZKFEcpHB4QSt0Qc-h_xIsxvIRv2cUMkOO16XsPnG5k3yjfbjLRZ_vJdcJqC6AJKzA4CKBI/4pe/uP3EnI-NQK2tTC0xqvcYjg/h1/h001.4DnG5BAZNIUWfVj_6EecIpYLBtC1dUbw1fPoJTNrVOo)** Let’s be real about this race, Peter: PA-03 is one of the bluest districts in the country, and this is the first open seat in 35 years. Whoever wins the Democratic primary is very likely to go to Congress. **So this race is less about whether****a Democrat wins — and more about**** _what kind_****.** Across the country, we’ve seen too many politicians campaign like they’re with working people, only to fall in line with corporate interests once they’re in office. They say the right things, then govern like lobbyists are calling the shots. **That’s not the kind of leadership Philly stands for, and it’s not what this moment demands.** We’re fighting for a country where people can afford to stay in their homes, get the care they need, and live with dignity. That means taxing the wealthy, closing corporate loopholes, and building real governing power rooted in working-class communities, from City Hall to Congress. **Chris Rabb is part of that fight.** He’s taken on corporate power, pushed bold policies, and stood with communities often ignored. Representing a majority-Black, mixed-income district in Northwest Philly, he brings that same commitment to everything he does: putting community over profit, defending workers, and making sure housing, healthcare, and clean air aren't treated as luxuries. **And what we’re building in Philly doesn’t stay in Philly, Peter.** When we win in a city like ours — one of the largest in the country — it sends a message everywhere: working people don’t have to settle. But wins like that don’t just happen. **They’re built by calling voters, texting folks across the district, knocking on doors in every neighborhood, and making sure people know exactly who Chris is and what he’s fighting for.****_That’s_****the work in front of us.** [**If you’re with us, chip in and help power this campaign. clean_body: | | | Hey Peter, We’re Kendra Brooks and Nicolas O’Rourke — At-Large Philadelphia City Councilmembers elected on the Working Families Party ballot line. A few years ago, we proved what happens when working people organize and refuse to play by the rules written for us. We knocked off the Republicans and became Philly’s dominant minority party — not with big money, but with people power, block by block. That’s how we move. So when there’s a chance to send someone to Congress from our city, in a district that runs through West Philly, Center City, South Philly, and North Philly, we take it seriously. That’s why we’re proud to share that the Working Families Party is endorsing Chris Rabb for Congress in Pennsylvania’s 3rd District. Let’s be real about this race, Peter: PA-03 is one of the bluest districts in the country, and this is the first open seat in 35 years. Whoever wins the Democratic primary is very likely to go to Congress. So this race is less about whethera Democrat wins — and more about what kind. Across the country, we’ve seen too many politicians campaign like they’re with working people, only to fall in line with corporate interests once they’re in office. They say the right things, then govern like lobbyists are calling the shots. That’s not the kind of leadership Philly stands for, and it’s not what this moment demands. We’re fighting for a country where people can afford to stay in their homes, get the care they need, and live with dignity. That means taxing the wealthy, closing corporate loopholes, and building real governing power rooted in working-class communities, from City Hall to Congress. Chris Rabb is part of that fight. He’s taken on corporate power, pushed bold policies, and stood with communities often ignored. body:
Why I'm all in on Francesca Hong
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260331-2670)
Peter,
My name is Nina Turner. I'm a former Ohio State Senator, the national co-chair of Bernie Sanders' presidential campaign, and a lifelong organizer who has spent my entire career fighting political corruption. I’m writing to you today because of a candidate in Wisconsin who is running on those same principles — and winning.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260331.jiZWXk&refcode=em20260331-2670&t=1&akid=2670%2E105371%2EqawhmL)
Francesca Hong is not another cautious, politics-as-usual Democrat waiting for permission to lead. She’s a service worker, a single mom, the daughter of immigrants, a small business owner and a State Representative, where she’s been a tireless fighter for working-class people. Now, she’s leading the Democratic field for governor running on the boldest affordability platform in the race.
Universal childcare — because no parent should have to choose between their job and their child. Paid family leave — because working people deserve to be there when their family needs them without losing their paycheck. Fully funded public schools — because the quality of our children’s education should not depend on their zip code. Expanded healthcare — because no one should go bankrupt for getting sick in the richest country on earth.
Fran's policies are universally popular, they will improve lives, and most importantly, Fran will fight to get it done. Her vision for creating permanent affordability in Wisconsin is resonating across party lines because voters are hungry for leadership that serves them, not corporations.
Wisconsin has the opportunity to play a pivotal role in showing the country what happens when we elect Democrats who prioritize working families.
**That’s why I’m calling on progressives everywhere to rally behind Fran and support her historic campaign. This is a once-in-a-lifetime chance to put a rock-solid candidate into the governor’s office of a crucial swing state.**
But she can't do it without resources. In a crowded primary against candidates with deeper donor networks and establishment backing, Fran is relying entirely on grassroots support. No corporate PAC money. Just people like you and me who believe the Democratic Party should fight for working families.
**[That's how we win — with a movement.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260331.jiZWXk&refcode=em20260331-2670&t=2&akid=2670%2E105371%2EqawhmL)**

In solidarity,
**Senator Nina Turner**
**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_fh_footer?refcode=em20260331-2670&t=22&refcode2=2670_105371_qawhmL&akid=2670%2E105371%2EqawhmL)**

https://emergeamerica.org/ [https://emergeamerica.org/]
Dear Peter,
What sets Emerge apart isn’t just that we train women to run for office, it’s how, when, and why we do it.
If we want more women in office, we can’t wait until the final weeks of a campaign, we have to invest at the very beginning. That’s how we expand the pool of candidates, build confidence, and prepare women to lead and win.
From our in-depth Signature Trainings to our accessible “Step Forward” sessions, Emerge meets women wherever they are and gives them the tools to take the next step.
But what truly makes Emerge different is what happens after the training ends.
We stay invested.
We build connections.
We open doors.
Because this work isn’t about one race—it’s about building a pipeline of leadership that lasts. And it’s working.
Today, more than 1,200 Emerge alums are serving in elected office across the country—shaping policy, representing their communities, and proving what’s possible when women are prepared to lead.
This is how we change the face of power. But none of it happens without you.
If you believe in building leaders—not just candidates—chip in today to power the next generation of Emerge women.

name: Kate Berry
subject: [LAST CHANCE] Help protect 200 acres today
body:
Dear Peter,

We are at a pivotal moment for the future of Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve.

If we can gather the funds needed, we can expand the reserve by 25% and permanently preserve 200 more acres of land. But we need your help to act now . [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

Make Your Gift Now [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

This expansion will allow us to secure previously unprotected old-growth redwoods and preserve an ecosystem that includes forests, grasslands, and critical wildlife habitats.

Just as importantly, we’re working with the Kashia Band of Pomo Indians to further enable public access to this redwood wonderland in ways that honor both the living culture of the Kashia and the traditions of Indigenous stewardship.

Something magical happens when people step foot into the reserve. Experiencing these redwoods first-hand inspires a special kind of love and appreciation. Our goal is to give more people these special experiences, while honoring the history of this land.

Make Your Gift Now [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

We don’t have much time left. It is urgent that we come together now to make this expansion possible. Will you make a special gift to help Save the Redwoods acquire these 200 acres and preserve these extraordinary forests forever? [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

With gratitude,
Kate Berry
Director of Annual Giving

P.S. Every acre we secure strengthens habitat connectivity, supports ongoing ecological research, and honors the cultural history of these special places. But we cannot secure this land without supporters like you stepping forward! [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

Photo by Coldwater Collective

Help restore and protect the redwoods
DONATE NOW [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

United States

subject: You’re not an ATM to me, friend.
body:
|
#
Friend, I want to start with something simple – and important: **You’re not an ATM to me.** Too many campaigns treat people like a transaction or a target. That’s not how I believe this work should be done, and it’s not how we’ve run this campaign from day one. If you’ve read a few of my emails before, I hope you’ve noticed the difference. We don’t rely on panic or scare tactics to get attention. We’re upfront about the stakes, honest about the work ahead, and respectful of people like you, who make this campaign possible. Because this campaign isn’t powered by fear and ALL CAPS messages that make you never want to donate to a campaign again – it’s powered by people who have hope for the future we’re building together, chipping in what they can, when they can. That grassroots support made it possible to win a Trump-won district and keep showing up for mid-Michigan – pushing for affordable health care, lower costs, and policies that actually improve people’s day-to-day lives. And it’s what’s going to help us protect this seat and win again in November. [**TONIGHT marks our first FEC fundraising deadline of the year. Now, with MI-08 being called the tipping-point seat in the fight to flip the House, grassroots support matters more than ever. | Friend,
---
I’m sick of seeing text messages that accuse you of abandoning the GOP after all you’ve done for us.
---
All because you didn’t give $15 before some random deadline, that’s supposed to mean you **_“betrayed”_** the Republican Party and became a Democrat?
---
So all the times you stood in line to vote, you knocked on doors, you put up a yard sign, you made phone calls, you filled out surveys, you sacrificed your time and money – suddenly, all of that means nothing?
---
**_Give me a break! That’s just insulting._**
---
_Hand to God, I will never stoop to that low._
---
Truth be told, I try not to write too many emails and texts as it is. I’m busy working in Washington to do the job you asked me to do.
---
Honestly, fundraising just isn’t Priority #1.
---
At the end of 2024, I transferred $2.5 MILLION _**away**_ from my own campaign to help conservatives in tough races who _truly_ needed help.
---
**You know what I care about most?** The _ONLY_ thing that WINS elections – **_VOTES_**.
---
_That means registering voters, verifying every Trump voter’s profile, and constantly getting LIVE feedback from voters like you so that the President and I _always_ have the best, most accurate data in the country._
---
That’s how we won in 2024. And it’s my plan to win AGAIN in 2026.
---
[**Please complete the brief questionnaire to verify that YOU are among the highest propensity voters we can count on in the midterms – and then I’ll officially mark you as “verified” in our GOP Voter file for the month.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

Jim Jordan

As Passover approaches, Connecticut should ask a simple question: why are our workers still stuck in tax bondage to New York?
The Exodus story is about labor, burden, and a ruler who would not let go. In a modern and obviously non-literal sense, that is the tension here. Connecticut residents live here, raise families here, pay property taxes here, and increasingly work here from home.
Yet, under New York's [convenience of the employer rule](https://substack.com/redirect/85111776-7d64-48ac-99f1-67c2fd629527?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), normal workdays spent at home can still be treated as New York workdays when the assigned office is in New York, unless the home office qualifies as a bona fide employer office. [Connecticut House Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/50952a74-8d94-4745-bd85-0c75ba45f9e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) argued this week that the result costs Connecticut more than $340 million a year.
# What About No Tax on Tips and Overtime?
Connecticut had a chance to respond on the worker side too. [HB 5010](https://substack.com/redirect/dda35714-d255-4e89-a046-921f2d7f4b6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would exempt tips, gratuities, and overtime pay from the Connecticut personal income tax. At the federal level, the IRS says workers may claim temporary deductions for qualified tips and qualified overtime for tax years 2025 through 2028, subject to limits and eligibility rules. _**Connecticut could have matched that pro-work direction at the state level and did not under the one-party rule of Hartford**_.
# A Win Win for the CT Democrats
And here is the sharper political contrast: _**Connecticut Democrats**_ should, at least in theory, love the enforcement side of this idea. Connecticut already requires employers that maintain an office or transact business here to register for withholding, and wages paid for services rendered in Connecticut are already subject to Connecticut withholding rules. _**So if an employer from any state regularly uses remote labor physically performed in Connecticut, the state could require that employer to[register](https://substack.com/redirect/c9d0d8c3-9ff3-40c0-9464-ddbb32f91ed5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), report Connecticut-based employees, count Connecticut workdays, and withhold accordingly. In other words: more registration, more reporting, more bureaucracy, and more protection for Connecticut's tax base.**_
# **If New York can tax your kitchen table, Connecticut can license your employer.**
The economic case is straightforward. Connecticut's economy is heavily service-based and increasingly dependent on professional, business, and other knowledge-sector work that can be performed from anywhere. That makes the state especially vulnerable when another jurisdiction claims tax rights over labor physically performed here. A registration-and-reporting rule would not necessarily raise conservatives' own tax bills; for many Connecticut residents, the main issue is which state gets the revenue, because Connecticut already has rules dealing with withholding on in-state work and credits for taxes paid elsewhere. **The bigger point is that Connecticut should stop passively exporting its tax base and $340 million comes back in to be put into the Budget.**
# This Policy is Good for the Environment - Everyone Wins
There is also an environmental and public-health argument. The whole policy push in recent years has been less commuting, less congestion, fewer emissions, and more work where people actually live. _**[EPA says air pollution can worsen asthma symptoms and that traffic-related pollution is linked to childhood asthma harms. EPA also says asthma disproportionately impacts minority children, especially in urban communities with high levels of air pollution.](https://substack.com/redirect/4c7408ac-f1b0-4cd3-bd38-63debfb44a79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_ So a tax rule that preserves incentives for unnecessary commuting is not just a tax issue. It is also a congestion issue, an emissions issue, and an asthma issue.
# Connecticut loves to regulate. Fine. Then regulate where it matters. Regulate the tax rolls.
Require out-of-state employers using Connecticut remote labor to register here, report here, and withhold here. That would protect Connecticut revenue, align tax policy with the remote-work economy, and reinforce the broader public goal of reducing unnecessary commuting and pollution.
_And the political irony is obvious: Democrats get more registration, more bureaucracy, and more income-tax enforcement, while conservatives do not need to pay more just to prove a point.**The state gets to defend its own tax base, and the economy, the environment and the children ALL come out ahead. There just has to be a provision against retaliation by the employer to suddenly force a remote worker to start commuting.**_
# **Thoughts Going Into Holy Week and Passover**
New York should stop collecting free tax money from Connecticut workers whose labor is physically performed in Connecticut.
_**From Pharaoh Hochul to payroll, enough is enough. Let CT people go from Tax On Labor Performed Here in the Constitution State. This would be a bi-partisan piece of legislation that Hartford can embrace.**_

Friends, when I was sworn in as your Attorney General, I made a promise to Californians that no matter what came our way, we would be ready.
And since the moment Donald Trump took office again in January of last year, we’ve been proving that.
Attorneys general across the country prepared for Trump 2.0 because our constituents deserved nothing less than complete readiness in the face of a lawless administration.
We knew we would face a flurry of executive overreach, an onslaught of unconstitutional actions, and unwavering attacks on the freedoms we’re sworn to uphold.

Tonight at midnight, Q1 fundraising numbers close.
Every donor, reporter, and party official will pull those numbers tomorrow morning to decide who's serious about flipping CA-45.
The margin last time was **653 votes**. I've been in this district every week since November — at the coffee shops, the community centers, the town halls. I'm building what it takes to win.
But I need our Q1 report to show we can do it.
## ⏰ DEADLINE: MIDNIGHT TONIGHT
Your gift today is counted in our official Q1 total — the number the whole party reads tomorrow.

With all of the chaos and destruction I see in Washington every day, gaining the support from our community gives me hope that when we come together to work towards a better future, we can deliver the progress that our communities deserve. But there’s still work to be done. We’ve raised 75% of our goal, but there are still a few hours left. This is about more than reaching a goal—this is about having the resources we need to win in November. Best, Doris Matsui As a Member of Congress, Doris works to ensure that the voices of her district’s constituents are heard in Congress, and fights for the needs of the Sacramento region. subject: This wasn’t the plan.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Maggie for NH
body:
I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128456396/611412020/-2000534896?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.03.31_Mark-Kelly_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP-NC_RS-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YjE2NDdhZS0yMjJkLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Oxg7VJLgm0UBVmMgnnjbNHnd8GzDNXZrcdIZ5EmXsJE=) Team, when Gabby and I first agreed that I would run for Senate back in 2019, we knew things would change. We know more than most how public service can change your life.

But I’ve got to tell you, I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy.

I know that service comes with risk, sure. But I didn’t set out to be threatened with a court-martial by the Secretary of Defense, or to have the President of the United States calling for my execution.

Look, I don’t want you to worry about me. I’ve been through a lot in my life, and things like this don’t intimidate me all that much.

I do worry that Trump might succeed at intimidating others, though. Like people just beginning to get involved, or thinking about joining a peaceful demonstration, or speaking out at a town hall. I worry Trump and his cronies are trying to scare people out of resisting him.

But then I see millions of people meeting this moment with the courage and resolve it demands of them. People like my friend Maggie Hassan. It makes me hopeful, sure. But more than that, it makes me incredibly proud.

We’re ready to fight like hell to save our democracy. If you’re with me, please:

All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy. = Team, when Gabby and I first agreed that I would run for Senate back in 2019, we knew things would change. We know more than most how public service can change your life. But I’ve got to tell you, I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy. I know that service comes with risk, sure. But I didn’t set out to be threatened with a court-martial by the Secretary of Defense, or to have the President of the United States calling for my execution. Look, I don’t want you to worry about me. I’ve been through a lot in my life, and things like this don’t intimidate me all that much. I do worry that Trump might succeed at intimidating others, though. Like people just beginning to get involved, or thinking about joining a peaceful demonstration, or speaking out at a town hall. I worry Trump and his cronies are trying to scare people out of resisting him. But then I see millions of people meeting this moment with the courage and resolve it demands of them. A personal note as we close out the quarter. Peter,

A little over a month ago, I officially filed to run for reelection.

Serving the people of St. Louis has been one of the greatest honors of my life. Together, we've made real progress protecting our communities, standing up for justice, and fighting for what matters most in MO-01 and all across our state.

But there's more work to do, and I know we can do it, **but not alone.** As we close out our first FEC quarter of the year, it's important that all of us who can step up and do our part to build a campaign we can all be proud of, and so I can continue serving you in Congress knowing that what we've built together is stronger than ever before.

And let me be clear: your support isn't just a donation, Peter.

It's a vote of confidence in our shared vision for St. Louis, and I'm determined to keep this momentum going full-speed ahead all the way through election day. And now, I’m carrying his legacy with me each and every single day.
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Ug1vqvBHglYDZbJNUBqWyQIwHZ1bNtW3_wkTATrqeVKI1uf3nDiDkwM4A0yBgjbig0jqMYJ3NtBSQPG0MDauIOzC7PUoI8XTsJy4I4vXHTAr0kx6CEecJXLF1fzXe-VY3bcmQR1GWMCxWtZDUBpmyhdizV3sqp2hDGHtSs5-CMWhUSdmTMi4yE3uDnYPZu6vp484S9BWboc_2nIbxdYe4Tv9lRntXztt&c=yS0RLBlmU0m3tYA74U_5mqpyu6Y2rEXQ1bfViH29BhGuc7Iaz0AS2w==&ch=WjrPdhJZM-1D3pJQVBDaBt3r0sREm3mMUaN5Gj-u5d2y39YStlSoTg==)

| Peter,
My grandfather was a sharecropper.
He worked the land from sunup to sundown that he would never own. He picked cotton by hand in the brutal Louisiana heat, breaking his body for a system designed to keep him exactly where he was -- poor, powerless, and dependent on the landowners who controlled everything.
That was life in the Louisiana Delta. My father grew up in that world. In those days in rural Louisiana, many boys left school early because their families needed them in the fields.
Work came first.
But my Dad had a dream that his son wouldn't have to live that way. That somehow, some way, our family would own land instead of working someone else's. That we'd build something that couldn't be taken away.
And he did it. Through decades of backbreaking work, he made that dream real.
We started with 220 acres my father had leased and built it into something real, something ours.
Today, we farm over 3,200 acres. 700 of those acres belong to my family outright.
Some of the same Louisiana delta soil my grandfather worked as a sharecropper -- my family owns it now.
Do you understand how profound that is? How impossible that would have seemed to my grandfather?
And now I'm running to become Louisiana's first Black senator since Reconstruction.
Sometimes I think about what my grandfather would say if he could see this moment. A man living in a system designed to keep him down, whose grandson might represent this entire state in the United States Senate.
It takes my breath away.
This isn't just about me. It's about every Black family in America that was told they'd never amount to anything. Every sharecropper's descendant who was supposed to stay in their place. Every person who was counted out before they even got started.
If I win this seat, it won't erase the centuries of injustice that came before. It won't undo what was done to my grandfather or the millions like him.
But it will prove something powerful: that in Louisiana -- in the Deep South -- we can move forward. That the grandson of a sharecropper can stand as an equal in the halls of power. That our democracy, for all its flaws, can still bend toward justice.
My grandfather never got to see this. My father -- God rest his soul -- never got to see this either.
But my grandkids will. And maybe, just maybe, they'll grow up in a Louisiana where anything truly is possible, regardless of the color of your skin or which side of the tracks you were born on.
That's what this campaign means to me. It's personal in a way I can barely put into words.
And I need your help to make it real.

But my Dad had a dream that his son wouldn't have to live that way. That somehow, some way, our family would own land instead of working someone else's. That we'd build something that couldn't be taken away. And he did it. Through decades of backbreaking work, he made that dream real. We started with 220 acres my father had leased and built it into something real, something ours. Today, we farm over 3,200 acres. 700 of those acres belong to my family outright. Some of the same Louisiana delta soil my grandfather worked as a sharecropper -- my family owns it now. Do you understand how profound that is? How impossible that would have seemed to my grandfather? And now I'm running to become Louisiana's first Black senator since Reconstruction. Sometimes I think about what my grandfather would say if he could see this moment. A man living in a system designed to keep him down, whose grandson might represent this entire state in the United States Senate. It takes my breath away. This isn't just about me. It's about every Black family in America that was told they'd never amount to anything. Every sharecropper's descendant who was supposed to stay in their place. Every person who was counted out before they even got started. If I win this seat, it won't erase the centuries of injustice that came before. It won't undo what was done to my grandfather or the millions like him. But it will prove something powerful: that in Louisiana -- in the Deep South -- we can move forward. That the grandson of a sharecropper can stand as an equal in the halls of power. That our democracy, for all its flaws, can still bend toward justice. My grandfather never got to see this. My father -- God rest his soul -- never got to see this either. But my grandkids will. And maybe, just maybe, they'll grow up in a Louisiana where anything truly is possible, regardless of the color of your skin or which side of the tracks you were born on. That's what this campaign means to me. It's personal in a way I can barely put into words. And I need your help to make it real. == If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | == | == | == | | | == | == | == | == | My grandfather picked cotton on land he'd never own. His grandson is running for the United States Senate. That's the promise of America. That's what we're fighting for. Billionaires are watching these numbers.
#
I’ll be direct.
Today is the **first major FEC fundraising deadline since a billionaire-backed opponent entered this race.**
And what we report at midnight will shape everything that comes next.
**Billionaires and corporate PACs are watching these numbers closely.** They want to see if they can overwhelm this campaign early.
So this moment matters.
**[I’m asking: will you chip in $1, $10, or whatever you can before the deadline?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22626?refcode=LN_20260331%3Frefcode%3Dem20260331-1601&t=1&akid=1601%2E2118727%2EM_9ct7)** Because right now, **the number of people who give is just as important as the total raised.**
**[DONATE NOW ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22626?refcode=LN_20260331%3Frefcode%3Dem20260331-1601&t=2&akid=1601%2E2118727%2EM_9ct7)**
Let me explain what’s happening.
I worked with Bernie Sanders to introduce a Billionaire Tax: a modest tax so the wealthiest pay their fair share to fund healthcare, housing, and education.
Now, the backlash is here.
A flood of outside money is pouring into this race from the same ultra-wealthy networks that try to buy elections across the country.
Political analysts are already calling this the toughest race I’ve faced.
But here’s what they don’t understand: This campaign isn’t powered by billionaires. It’s powered by people.
I don’t take corporate PAC money.
I don’t take checks from lobbyists.
And I’m not going to start now.
But to win, we have to prove that we have the grassroots strength to fight back and win.
So I’m asking one more time:
[**Can you make a donation of $1 or more before this FEC deadline?**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22626?refcode=LN_20260331%3Frefcode%3Dem20260331-1601&t=3&akid=1601%2E2118727%2EM_9ct7)
Every single contribution sends a message that this campaign belongs to working people, not the wealthy few.
**[DONATE NOW ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22626?refcode=LN_20260331%3Frefcode%3Dem20260331-1601&t=4&akid=1601%2E2118727%2EM_9ct7)**
Thank you for standing with me at this critical moment.
In solidarity,
Ro

name: Office of the First Lady
subject: News From First Lady Dawn Moore
body:
| | | | Hello Friends and Fellow Marylanders, This March, we focused on uplifting Maryland's women and children. We celebrated the extraordinary contributions of women around the world during Women’s History Month, created opportunities for our young people to embrace the power of reading through the #ReadMoreMaryland campaign, advocated to protect the public health of all Marylanders against psychoactive substances, and met with women leaders to discuss collaboration and advocacy around the most pressing issues impacting our nation. As First Lady, a lifelong public servant, and a mother of two wonderful children — these moments were personal for me. Everyday, I am proud to work in partnership with Marylanders across the state to make the change in our society that our future generations can be proud of. Our administration will continue to do the work, and we hope that you will join us! Take Care, **First Lady Dawn Moore** |
* * *
---
## **KEEPING UP WITH**
# **THE FIRST LADY**
### [First Lady Moore Launches #ReadMoreMaryland Campaign to Advance Literacy among Maryland Students](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fleadership%2Ffirstlady%2Fnews%2Fpages%2Ffirst-lady-moore-launches-readmoremaryland-campaign-advance-literacy-among-maryland-students.aspx/1/0100019d44eb30b0-be3b43a3-1034-477a-bfeb-728fb4f7443d-000000/7Y3upZzPOufNcBWMjQ6EUIHS_uuKfcBkK8jaA2keZaI=451)
During National Reading Month, First Lady Dawn Moore launched the #ReadMoreMaryland campaign, a statewide literacy campaign aimed to inspire Maryland students to read. In partnership with the [Governor’s Office for Children](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgoc.maryland.gov%2FPages%2Fhome.aspx/1/0100019d44eb30b0-be3b43a3-1034-477a-bfeb-728fb4f7443d-000000/WhEegfIdPvXxLs51kLabsRAtORvZvl_kmp3GbjLHrMA=451) and the [Maryland State Department of Education](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.marylandpublicschools.org%2FPages%2FDefault.aspx/1/0100019d44eb30b0-be3b43a3-1034-477a-bfeb-728fb4f7443d-000000/lfOmkxZxU8C1Ko-wbI3XD9FJiYbnyJChKtqQMhFvhac=451), the campaign reinforces the Moore-Miller Administration’s commitment to education and advancing literacy among our Maryland students.
The campaign received an overwhelming response from students across the state — from parent organizations in Baltimore City, churches on the Eastern Shore, local schools, and public libraries. Next month, five young Marylanders and their families will be invited to Annapolis to show off their book to First Lady Moore.
Since taking office, the Moore-Miller Administration has invested record funding in Maryland’s K-12 education system. In the last two years, Maryland has seen reading scores increase in nearly every grade — moving from 40th to 20th in the nation for literacy. The state has also seen graduation rates rise and teacher vacancy rates cut in half. In January, the governor announced a record $10.2 billion investment in public schools as part of his Fiscal Year 2027 budget proposal.
* * *
---
### [First Lady Moore Testifies Before Senate Finance Committee in Support of Legislation to Protect Public Health of Marylanders Against Psychoactive Substances](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/http:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fleadership%2Ffirstlady%2Fnews%2Fpages%2Ffirst-lady-moore-testifies-senate-finance-committee-support-legislation-protect-public-health-marylanders-psychoactive-subs.aspx/1/0100019d44eb30b0-be3b43a3-1034-477a-bfeb-728fb4f7443d-000000/2AGGqD4iPwZ2O4BZhjEUCbGJ69VTC7bhOupVKhSMheE=451)
First Lady Dawn Moore testified in front of the Senate Finance Committee in support of [Senate Bill 820](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fmgaleg.maryland.gov%2Fmgawebsite%2FLegislation%2FDetails%2FSB0820%3Fys=2026RS/1/0100019d44eb30b0-be3b43a3-1034-477a-bfeb-728fb4f7443d-000000/ZK26B0PzF1xwOnphHoRH6GcyFjlt5jVIN4n8LAIg-cQ=451), which enforces strict state-level controls to protect the public health of all Marylanders against psychoactive substances associated with dangerous side effects. Sponsored by Senator Antonio Hayes, the bill will enforce consumer protection measures for certain psychoactive substances — prohibiting retailers from employing deceptive marketing practices geared toward children to sell them.
To protect children, the legislation authorizes the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to enforce prohibitions on the sale of products containing kratom and phenibut to anyone under the age of 21, and strictly bans predatory marketing tactics — including use of cartoons, superheroes, and neon-colored packaging — specifically designed to appeal to minors. By enforcing requirements for transparent labeling and prohibiting unverified therapeutic claims, the bill aims to eliminate the gas station loophole that allows highly addictive synthetics to be sold alongside energy drinks and candy in grocery stores.
* * *
---
### **[Governor and First Lady Moore Host 2026 Women's Hall of Fame Induction](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.flickr.com%2Fphotos%2Fmdgovpics%2Falbums%2F72177720332833653%2F/1/0100019d44eb30b0-be3b43a3-1034-477a-bfeb-728fb4f7443d-000000/geqHlH52z14YF-zCQBbtKognzbtqiYJkQFbLGR1xYmA=451)**
Governor and First Lady Moore honored eight women inducted into the Maryland Women's Hall of Fame at Government House.
This year's inductees include: former Maryland State Senator Delores Kelley; pioneering advocate for women’s reproductive health Dr. Sharon Camp (posthumously); The Center for Law and Social Policy Executive Director Wendy Chun-Hoon; trailblazing biophysicist Dr. Margaret Oakley Dayhoff (posthumously); entrepreneur and community advocate Elda Devarie; U.S. Army 2nd Lt. Emily J.T. Perez (posthumously); Maryland Democratic Party former chair Susan Turnbull; and former Baltimore first lady and community advocate Nancy Lombardi D’Alesandro (posthumously).
The room was filled with distinguished guests including Lt. Governor Aruna Miller; Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi, who honored her mother inductee Nancy Lombardi D’Alesandro; members of the General Assembly; Moore-Miller administration cabinet members; and families of the inductees.
Established in 1985, the Maryland Women’s Hall of Fame in partnership between the [Maryland Commission for Women](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fdhs.maryland.gov%2Fmaryland-commission-women%2F/1/0100019d44eb30b0-be3b43a3-1034-477a-bfeb-728fb4f7443d-000000/sOpoi0ip04OSh6t_558gHcy8jVl0uRS7SOEk6k-rYCk=451) and the Women Legislators of Maryland memorializes and honors Maryland women whose lives and work are of historic significance to the health, economic, political, and cultural history of the state.

As First Lady, a lifelong public servant, and a mother of two wonderful children — these moments were personal for me. The state has also seen graduation rates rise and teacher vacancy rates cut in half. First Lady Dawn Moore testified in front of the Senate Finance Committee in support of , which enforces strict state-level controls to protect the public health of all Marylanders against psychoactive substances associated with dangerous side effects. Sponsored by Senator Antonio Hayes, the bill will enforce consumer protection measures for certain psychoactive substances — prohibiting retailers from employing deceptive marketing practices geared toward children to sell them. **" New Texas THC rules start tomorrow. What's actually banned?"** [Austin American-Statesman's](https://substack.com/redirect/2116471e-048e-4516-bf8f-df0f3fbe0279?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Faith Bugenhagen** - A ban on smokable hemp will take effect on March 31 under newly proposed and approved guidelines.

Newly adopted regulations on THC, which will effectively ban the sale of smokable hemp and extracts, are set to take effect March 31 -- leaving Texas retailers and consumers one last day to prepare for sweeping changes.

The Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) adopted a finalized version of previously proposed regulations in early March, aligning with Gov. **Greg Abbott** 's executive order cracking down on hemp.

The new rules take effect Tuesday, March 31.

How will THC laws change under the new regulations?

The new regulations prohibit the sale of smokable hemp and certain extracts by altering how the DSHS measures delta-9 THC, a cannabinoid that produces cannabis' intoxicating effects.

Under the current state statute, cannabis with no more than 0.3% delta-9 by dry weight is considered legal hemp.

The adopted guidelines include a new "total THC" standard, which counts THCA, a naturally occurring cannabinoid in raw cannabis, toward the legal THC limit.

(_[AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/ea0a0631-667b-4102-ba38-b6909f0ee41c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

Three agencies -- the **China Grove Police Department** , the **St. Hedwig Marshal 's Office** and the **Hollywood Park Police Department** -- are the most recent municipal agencies to enter agreements with ICE under the 287(g) program.

They join the Texas Department of Public Safety, the Precinct 3 Bexar County constable's office and the Balcones Heights Police Department, which entered into the same agreements in January.

The program, established through the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1996, allows ICE to train and authorize state and local law enforcement officers to assist with certain immigration enforcement functions.

**" Another Dallas real estate fiasco"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/62467417-281f-4cfb-8210-cea45fad6254?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - The plan seemed reasonable. Dallas would use bond and COVID relief funds to buy or renovate a vacant hospital and four aging motels into transitional and permanent supportive housing for homeless individuals and families. The five projects would provide 680 new beds for these vulnerable Dallasites.

About five years later, only two properties are complete: one that the city bought and remodeled and another it helped a nonprofit purchase and renovate. Another hotel that the city acquired was ready to start construction but stalled last year because of unexpected changes in federal funding.

The final two are simply losses. The 12-acre hospital site, located at 2929 S. Hampton Road in Oak Cliff and purchased in 2022, is being sold. Relentless community opposition and tone-deaf city leadership at the time doomed the project from the start.
The last property, a derelict extended-stay hotel on Independence Drive, backs up to Interstate 20 and sits between other declining motels. (_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/5b16a318-f5ee-48b0-b9f8-f43861761fff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

TOP NEWS " Federal trial over air conditioning in Texas prisons starts with dispute over alleged heat-related deaths" Alex Nguyen - There were allegedly five heat-related deaths over the last two summers in Texas prisons, the plaintiff's attorneys presented on the first day of the federal trial over insufficient air conditioning in these facilities. The Texas Department of Criminal Justice has not publicly acknowledged heat as a significant factor in these deaths, and the state's attorneys also pushed back against these claims during the Monday proceeding. The hearing in Austin followed a March 2025 ruling from U.S. District Judge Robert Pitman that said housing Texas prison inmates in sweltering facilities that lack air conditioning is "plainly unconstitutional." The Obama appointee declined at the time to force TDCJ to immediately install temporary or permanent air conditioning, which the agency said could cost more than $1 billion. () " NASA countdown begins for first crewed moon mission in decades" via - The countdown to NASA's next mission to the moon is officially underway, marking a major step toward sending astronauts back for the first time in decades. A crewed launch is now just days away, and over the next two days, teams will run through critical checks to make sure everything is ready for liftoff. The countdown begins later today, kicking off a 49-hour process to prepare both the rocket and crew for launch. Astronauts arrived at Kennedy Space Center on Friday and are now entering the final phase before liftoff. Launch is scheduled for Wednesday evening, when the crew will board the Orion spacecraft atop a 322-foot-tall Space Launch System rocket. This mission will mark the first time humans fly this new system and the first crewed mission toward the moon in more than five decades. NASA says the mission is designed as a test flight to push the spacecraft to its limits. () " Texas Water Strain Raises Questions for Data Center Boom" via - A deepening water crisis in Corpus Christi, Texas, is raising questions about how to sustain growth in water-stressed regions as new, resource-intensive industries--including data centers--expand. Projections from city officials show Corpus Christi is approaching triggering emergency water measures, with supply projected to fall short of demand within 180 days by May. City officials and researchers say the shortfall isn't tied to data center development, but to prolonged drought and years of limited water use. Still, the crunch comes as Texas leaders push to attract more development, including artificial intelligence data centers. () " Student shoots a teacher at Texas high school before fatally shooting self, authorities say" via AP -- A 15-year-old student shot a teacher at a Texas high school and then fatally shot himself Monday, according to authorities, who were still investigating what led to the early morning attack. No other injuries were reported at Hill Country College Preparatory High School in Bulverde, a small but growing city near San Antonio. The teacher was taken to a nearby hospital. Comal County Sheriff Mark Reynolds said hours after the shooting that he did not know her condition. "What happened today is something no community ever wants to face, but we prepare for something that we hope never occurs," Reynolds said. He said the student shot the teacher before turning the gun on himself. Reynolds said investigators were working to understand the relationship between the student and the teacher and looking into how the firearm was obtained. The small campus of roughly 250 students was placed on lockdown shortly after 8:30 a.m., according to the school. One student told San Antonio television station that they heard loud bangs coming from a room on the second floor and then heard screaming. Another student told the TV station that she heard five shots and yelling before her debate teacher told students to get inside a classroom. Students were bused to a nearby middle school, where parents stood in long lines, some praying, as they waited to be reunited. Reynolds said the family members of the shooter had also gone into reunification line. "We're trying to collect as much information as we can from witnesses," Reynolds said. () " Who are the Homietos? Inside Houston's latest biker gang case" John Wayne Ferguson - A major gang indictment announced in Houston this month brought federal murder charges against members of the Homietos motorcycle gang. The organized crime indictment accused three members of the gang of participating in the fatal shooting of three people in 2023. Fifteen other gang members were accused of participating in assaults and firearms crimes. All of the allegations are tied to a central argument: that the men conspired to advance the Homietos' power and control. The charges are the latest example of the FBI's crackdown on area motorcycle gangs, which the agency said waged a bloody war on the streets of Houston in recent years. The Homietos are a motorcycle group founded in the Houston area that now has members in multiple states across the South and Midwest. () 2026 " Democrats Can't Turn Texas Blue--but Republicans Can" Mene Ukueberuwa - Democrats' dream of turning Texas blue has been a running joke in the Lone Star State for at least a dozen years. That's how long it's been since they nominated Wendy Davis , who became a fleeting progressive icon by protesting for abortion, as their champion to reclaim the governorship. Davis got blown out, and since then, Democratic candidates for governor and Senate have, at best, gotten close--despite their engineered hype from national media and loads of cash from outside donors. Democrats haven't won a statewide race in Texas in more than three decades, and it seems that the only way they can gain ground is if Republicans let them. So guess what Republicans are thinking about doing? The primary elections earlier this month were bad news for the GOP's odds in November, because aggressive and unserious Republicans overperformed in so many of them. In the headliner race for a Senate nomination, attorney general Ken Paxton finished within one point of sitting senator John Cornyn and forced a run-off election set for May 26. Paxton's good showing suggests that many primary voters aren't focused on winning. () " Voting rights groups sue Texas over alleged illegal voter purge" None - A group of voting and civil rights organizations is suing Texas, saying the state used flawed data and unfair methods to flag and potentially remove eligible voters from its rolls. The lawsuit, filed by the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) and other organizations, challenges a voter review process launched by the Texas Secretary of State's Office in October 2025. At the time, Secretary of State Jane Nelson said her office had compared the state's voter registration list of more than 18 million registered voters against a federal immigration database -- the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements, or SAVE system -- and identified 2,724 registered voters as potential noncitizens. Counties were then directed to investigate those voters' eligibility. It's unclear whether any voters have been removed from the rolls as a result of the state's findings. The Texas Secretary of State's Office declined to comment on Monday. () " In effort to turn Texas blue, Democratic nominees for statewide office are holding joint rallies" via - With President Trump's approval rating underwater and the chance of scandal-plagued Attorney General Ken Paxton to be the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate, Texas Democrats feel that the 2026 midterms present their best chance to win a statewide election in years. It has been 32 years since a Democrat won statewide office. The last time they came close was in 2018, when Beto O'Rourke lost the U.S. Senate race to Sen. Ted Cruz by just 2.6 percentage points. In an effort to boost their chances in 2026, Texas Democrats have launched Texas Together, a series of joint rallies supporting multiple statewide candidates. The first one took place earlier this month in Fort Worth. State Rep. James Talarico , the nominee for U.S. Senate, and state Rep. Gina Hinojosa , the nominee for governor, were among those who addressed hundreds of supporters. Before the event, Hinojosa spoke with CBS News Texas political reporter Jack Fink and explained why she felt it was important to rally with the party's other nominees. () " GOP mega donors back Bo French for Texas oil regulation seat" Carlos Nogueras Ramos, Dan Keemahill - A political action committee funded by Texas' most prolific hardline conservative donors was the main benefactor to Bo French 's campaign for the Texas Railroad Commission in the March Republican primary, spending $375,000 to bolster his bid. The Texas Freedom Fund for the Advancement of Justice, formerly known as Defend Texas Liberty, gave French $225,000 and spent another $150,000 on an ad promoting his candidacy in a widely circulated conservative newsletter. The two PACs have been predominantly financed by West Texas oil billionaires Tim Dunn and Farris Wilks , who have deployed tens of millions of dollars to pull the Texas GOP and Legislature toward their hardline, anti-LGBTQ+ and immigration stances. Dunn and Wilks' PAC accounted for more than half of the $637,139 French raised from the start of his campaign through late February, helping him secure a spot in the May runoff against incumbent Jim Wright. The winner will face Democrat Jon Rosenthal in November for one of the three seats on the commission, which regulates Texas' oil and gas industry. () " 2 Democrats, Letitia Plummer and Annise Parker, in 2026 runoff for Harris County judge nomination" via - In 57 days, voters across Texas will head back to the polls to vote in several runoff elections. In southeast Texas, the ballots for both parties include candidates for Harris County Judge. Two women, former Houston City Council member Letitia Plummer and former Houston mayor Annise Parker , will face off in a May 26th runoff for Harris County judge. This result follows incumbent judge Lina Hidalgo's announcement that she will not seek re-election in 2026. Plummer was elected twice to the Houston City Council. Plummer, a practicing dentist, wants to take what she calls an inclusive approach to Harris County. "I really felt like I was that progressive voice on city council," Plummer told ABC13. "I felt like our community needed a more progressive voice and someone who really understood the challenges that people, everyday people, are experiencing." () " Meet housing activist Maureen Galindo, who rode a shoestring campaign to a high-profile congressional runoff" Andrea Drusch - How Maureen Galindo went from a housing activist to a TX35 runoff When a new owner started making improvements to Maureen Galindo's downtown apartment complex in 2017, she saw an opportunity to put her community psychology training to work. Then a 31-year-old single mom, she'd just finished the courses for a master's program in Portland focused on improving the health of underserved communities, and moved her three small children to San Antonio where they could live more affordably. Months after moving into their $830 per month apartment, however, a massive public redevelopment project on San Pedro Creek had already started to spur change in the neighborhood, putting Galindo at the forefront of an affordable housing fight that would later become the topic of her master's thesis -- and shape her trajectory for the next decade to come. Last month Galindo shocked political watchers by finishing first in Democrats' primary for a brand-new congressional district in Southwest San Antonio -- outperforming the national party's favored candidate Johnny Garcia , who she'll now face in a May 26 primary runoff. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Restrictions on SNAP food benefits go into effect in Texas starting April 1" via - Starting April 1, new restrictions from the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) will take effect and will limit what can be purchased through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The new restrictions come after Senate Bill 379 was signed into law last summer. The U.S. Department of Agriculture Food and Nutrition Service approved a healthy foods waiver submitted by Texas, allowing the state to carry out the limitations. Some local residents who benefit from the San Antonio Food Bank often rely on SNAP. Food bank CEO Eric Cooper said it's important for his organization to educate their SNAP recipients on the changes. "You don't want the participant to feel stigma, or shame, or less than," said Cooper. "And at the point of this waiver going into place on April 1, I think there's going to be some education misses." Cooper said they're prepared with pass-along cards, flyers, and information to help inform those affected by the new restrictions. () " There will soon be new requirements to get hunting and fishing licenses in Texas" via - There will soon be new requirements to get hunting and fishing licenses in the state of Texas. The Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission approved new proof-of-residency requirements, according to a news release posted on the TPWD website. The agency said the update is aimed at cracking down on people who claim Texas residency to score cheaper license prices. The changes take effect Aug. 1, just two weeks before annual hunting and fishing licenses go on sale Aug. 15. Officials say the goal is simple: stop fraud and make sure only eligible buyers are getting resident discounts and benefits. For Texans and residents of most other states, the process stays relatively straightforward. You'll just need to show a valid, unexpired driver license or personal ID when buying a license through the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department. () " New Texas THC rules start tomorrow. What's actually banned?" Faith Bugenhagen - A ban on smokable hemp will take effect on March 31 under newly proposed and approved guidelines. Newly adopted regulations on THC, which will effectively ban the sale of smokable hemp and extracts, are set to take effect March 31 -- leaving Texas retailers and consumers one last day to prepare for sweeping changes. The Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) adopted a finalized version of previously proposed regulations in early March, aligning with Gov. Greg Abbott 's executive order cracking down on hemp. The new rules take effect Tuesday, March 31. How will THC laws change under the new regulations? The new regulations prohibit the sale of smokable hemp and certain extracts by altering how the DSHS measures delta-9 THC, a cannabinoid that produces cannabis' intoxicating effects. Under the current state statute, cannabis with no more than 0.3% delta-9 by dry weight is considered legal hemp. The adopted guidelines include a new "total THC" standard, which counts THCA, a naturally occurring cannabinoid in raw cannabis, toward the legal THC limit. () #TXLEGE " Could parts of New Mexico become Texas? Lawmakers are exploring it" John C. Moritz - The study ordered last week by House Speaker Dustin Burrows to examine whether Texas could actually gobble up some of the counties on the eastern rim of New Mexico has some political figures seeing red. Republican red. Burrows, R-Lubbock, is following up on a proposal being floated in the New Mexico Legislature that would allow counties in the state that share a border with Texas to, in effect, switch sides. And it just so happens that every one of those counties voted overwhelmingly for Donald Trump in 2024, while New Mexico as a whole gave its five electoral votes to Democrat Kamala Harris by a comfortable 52%-46% margin. Let's make clear from the outset that the annexation by Texas of one or more of the five counties looks iffy at best. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " More Bexar County law enforcement quietly enter ICE agreements" Diego Medel - Amid a backdrop of state, county and city officials voicing opposition to a planned U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention facility in San Antonio, smaller law enforcement agencies across Bexar County are quietly expanding their role in federal immigration enforcement. Three agencies -- the China Grove Police Department , the St. Hedwig Marshal 's Office and the Hollywood Park Police Department -- are the most recent municipal agencies to enter agreements with ICE under the 287(g) program. They join the Texas Department of Public Safety, the Precinct 3 Bexar County constable's office and the Balcones Heights Police Department, which entered into the same agreements in January. The program, established through the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1996, allows ICE to train and authorize state and local law enforcement officers to assist with certain immigration enforcement functions. Participation is voluntary, and the level of authority granted to local agencies depends on the type of agreement they enter into. () " How a San Antonio middle school got around budget cuts to keep its in-person tutoring program" Xochilt Garcia - How a San Antonio school saved its tutoring program from cuts When Gerald Lopez found out Sul Ross Middle School might replace its in-person student tutoring program with a virtual option due to funding cuts, he immediately jumped into action. Using his connections as a current Alamo Community Colleges District trustee, a former Northside Independent School District board member and a mentor for students at Sul Ross, he picked up the phone to ask around. "We don't need a computer system to tutor our students. We need real people," he recalled thinking when he heard the news. "We need young, energetic students wanting to better themselves and also better their community." Lopez found a solution: community work-study through Alamo Colleges, a way for students eligible for work-study under the federal student aid program to work off-campus, benefitting employers who can't afford to hire them on their own. Now, Sul Ross has two student tutors from Northwest Vista College and is still hiring for a couple more. () " Another Dallas real estate fiasco" via - The plan seemed reasonable. Dallas would use bond and COVID relief funds to buy or renovate a vacant hospital and four aging motels into transitional and permanent supportive housing for homeless individuals and families. The five projects would provide 680 new beds for these vulnerable Dallasites. About five years later, only two properties are complete: one that the city bought and remodeled and another it helped a nonprofit purchase and renovate. Another hotel that the city acquired was ready to start construction but stalled last year because of unexpected changes in federal funding. The final two are simply losses. The 12-acre hospital site, located at 2929 S. Hampton Road in Oak Cliff and purchased in 2022, is being sold. Relentless community opposition and tone-deaf city leadership at the time doomed the project from the start. The last property, a derelict extended-stay hotel on Independence Drive, backs up to Interstate 20 and sits between other declining motels. I’m running for Congress because science should have a seat at the table.

This administration is spreading lies about proven vaccines. They’re trying to cut healthcare. They’re sowing division, ignoring data, and spreading misinformation – putting lives at risk.
I’ve had enough – and that’s why I’m running for Congress. But I need your help to separate ourselves as the pro-science candidate in this race. I’ve set a goal of 100 grassroots donations by tonight’s end-of-month deadline to help us spread our pro-science message all across the district.

As a microbiologist, I’ve dedicated my career to fighting for evidence-based policy. I’ve seen firsthand how accurate information saves lives — and how misinformation costs them.
In Congress, I’ll make sure we base decisions on science rather than turning facts into partisan fights.
But it’s going to take a lot of work to get that done. We need all the grassroots help we can get to compete with Republican mega-donors and corporate PACs.
Make a grassroots contribution before tonight’s deadline to help us hit our goal, win this election, and give science, truth, and evidence a seat at the table. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260331em]

**" Federal trial over air conditioning in Texas prisons starts with dispute over alleged heat-related deaths"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/a1301980-09c0-4db6-8064-7ed32f2e41a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Alex Nguyen** - There were allegedly five heat-related deaths over the last two summers in Texas prisons, the plaintiff's attorneys presented on the first day of the federal trial over insufficient air conditioning in these facilities.

The Texas Department of Criminal Justice has not publicly acknowledged heat as a significant factor in these deaths, and the state's attorneys also pushed back against these claims during the Monday proceeding.

The hearing in Austin followed a March 2025 ruling from U.S. District Judge **Robert Pitman** that said housing Texas prison inmates in sweltering facilities that lack air conditioning is "plainly unconstitutional." The Obama appointee declined at the time to force TDCJ to immediately install temporary or permanent air conditioning, which the agency said could cost more than $1 billion. **" NASA countdown begins for first crewed moon mission in decades"** via [KHOU](https://substack.com/redirect/e94e7917-15fa-4bda-8483-16da33ee70f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - The countdown to NASA's next mission to the moon is officially underway, marking a major step toward sending astronauts back for the first time in decades.

A crewed launch is now just days away, and over the next two days, teams will run through critical checks to make sure everything is ready for liftoff.

The countdown begins later today, kicking off a 49-hour process to prepare both the rocket and crew for launch.

Astronauts arrived at Kennedy Space Center on Friday and are now entering the final phase before liftoff.

Launch is scheduled for Wednesday evening, when the crew will board the Orion spacecraft atop a 322-foot-tall Space Launch System rocket.

This mission will mark the first time humans fly this new system and the first crewed mission toward the moon in more than five decades.

NASA says the mission is designed as a test flight to push the spacecraft to its limits. (_[KHOU](https://substack.com/redirect/4878de17-02e6-4ee3-8b77-0ba0a368423a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Texas Water Strain Raises Questions for Data Center Boom"** via [Bloomberg Law](https://substack.com/redirect/ba832463-f8ca-4ab9-a29d-918a925c64c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - A deepening water crisis in Corpus Christi, Texas, is raising questions about how to sustain growth in water-stressed regions as new, resource-intensive industries--including data centers--expand.

Projections from city officials show Corpus Christi is approaching triggering emergency water measures, with supply projected to fall short of demand within 180 days by May.

City officials and researchers say the shortfall isn't tied to data center development, but to prolonged drought and years of limited water use.

Still, the crunch comes as Texas leaders push to attract more development, including artificial intelligence data centers. (_[Bloomberg Law News](https://substack.com/redirect/0d6c7cdf-771e-4e6f-a970-88c54d20a400?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Student shoots a teacher at Texas high school before fatally shooting self, authorities say"** via AP -- A 15-year-old student shot a teacher at a Texas high school and then fatally shot himself Monday, according to authorities, who were still investigating what led to the early morning attack.

No other injuries were reported at Hill Country College Preparatory High School in Bulverde, a small but growing city near San Antonio.

The teacher was taken to a nearby hospital. Comal County Sheriff Mark Reynolds said hours after the shooting that he did not know her condition.

"What happened today is something no community ever wants to face, but we prepare for something that we hope never occurs," Reynolds said.

He said the student shot the teacher before turning the gun on himself. Reynolds said investigators were working to understand the relationship between the student and the teacher and looking into how the firearm was obtained.

The small campus of roughly 250 students was placed on lockdown shortly after 8:30 a.m., according to the school. One student told San Antonio television station [KSAT](https://substack.com/redirect/709c143f-8cc0-4dce-a2a6-84d1658a3fa4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that they heard loud bangs coming from a room on the second floor and then heard screaming.

Another student told the TV station that she heard five shots and yelling before her debate teacher told students to get inside a classroom.

Students were bused to a nearby middle school, where parents stood in long lines, some praying, as they waited to be reunited. Reynolds said the family members of the shooter had also gone into reunification line.

"We're trying to collect as much information as we can from witnesses," Reynolds said. ([AP](https://substack.com/redirect/f8461c8b-860e-4713-83d0-3a1bfd734aaa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))

**" Who are the Homietos? Inside Houston's latest biker gang case"** [Houston Chronicle's](https://substack.com/redirect/486999bd-ffa5-40d5-9b04-407f3ab9361b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **John Wayne Ferguson** - A major gang indictment announced in Houston this month brought federal murder charges against members of the Homietos motorcycle gang.

The organized crime indictment accused three members of the gang of participating in the fatal shooting of three people in 2023. Fifteen other gang members were accused of participating in assaults and firearms crimes. All of the allegations are tied to a central argument: that the men conspired to advance the Homietos' power and control.

The charges are the latest example of the FBI's crackdown on area motorcycle gangs, which the agency said waged a bloody war on the streets of Houston in recent years.

The Homietos are a motorcycle group founded in the Houston area that now has members in multiple states across the South and Midwest. (_[HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/3399ca6f-ee28-4544-982f-bc89a0a07912?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)
