#
Can we be real with you for a moment?
We understand that a constant stream of emails asking for a contribution can sometimes get on your nerves. That’s okay.
**This email wasn't generated by AI**. **It was written by a real person**. We understand how people can get frustrated. _But let us explain why this is vital._
When we ask for your support, we don’t expect every person to give. But we ask because we know that when you can support the cause, you will. That’s how this transformative movement works:**by a whole lot of people doing their part to make something great.**
[The only way we can get there is through the support of small-dollar donors chipping in whatever they can. If you can, will you make a $3 contribution — or $5, or anything you can — right now? It’ll go a long way.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260331.rf1sU3&refcode=em20260331-11092-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=11092%2E2526796%2EQQZAOd)

We’re not exaggerating. Most members of Congress fuel their reelection campaigns by dedicating hours of their time asking rich donors for $500, $1000, or even $3500 donations.
**Alexandria is different.** This whole movement is fueled by online contributions like the ones we’re asking for in this email. With these contributions, we’ve built a campaign that is...
1. Raising resources, recruiting volunteers, and making calls to help elect progressive allies across Congress, and build a progressive majority.
2. Reaching out to communities across NY-14 and the country to fight for working people and support progressive candidates.
3. Raising money for community relief organizations, closing critical resources gaps that the federal government has left unfilled.
4. Working day and night to reelect AOC, defeat our Democratic primary challengers _and_ our Republican opponents, and **show the world what we can do**.

[If this movement is the model of what you want in our politics, please donate today to help us reach our end-of-quarter fundraising goal. ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260331.rf1sU3&refcode=em20260331-11092-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=11092%2E2526796%2EQQZAOd)

Team AOC

| | If your birth year starts with 19 instead of 20, you might remember _email forwarding chains_. The kind that promised good fortune if you sent it to 100 people (or terrible luck if you didn’t). **“I hate chain mail, but this one REALLY WORKS!” ** Tonight at midnight, this financial quarter closes, and soon our fundraising numbers from January 1st through March 31st will be public. Political donors, endorsing organizations, party committees, and opponents all treat it like a report card. For a grassroots campaign, these filings can be vulnerable and a little bit scary, especially when they compare hard-earned contributions to the millions of dollars poured into so-called “flip” districts. **Today, we’re asking you for something that no amount of money can buy.** If this campaign has earned your support – will you share this email with your people? Every forwarded message with your name on it is worth more than any ad we could buy. Six hundred volunteers didn't find this campaign through an algorithm. They found it through somebody they knew saying "You’ve been wanting to do something about everything that’s happening. You should check out Michaela Barnett’s campaign.” You could be that person today. **Will you forward this email to 2, 5, or even 10 people you know?** When you do, just tell them what's on your mind — what you're worried about, what you're hoping for — and why you think Michaela is the right person to represent us in D.C. We can’t promise luck or financial fortune tied to how many forwards you send, but we can promise you that spreading the word gives this campaign the BEST CHANCE to flip this seat! **→ Did you get an email forwarded from someone you trust? Start here: ** Michaela Barnett is a scientist, small business owner, and who worked in Congress. She's running against Tim Burchett to flip Tennessee's 2nd Congressional District — the longest-held Republican district in the country. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. Friend, let me level with you.
I know messages like these can be annoying, but we need to send them. Don't worry, I'll make this quick.
I'm asking for your support before our midnight deadline because I believe in people power.
I chose to run a campaign funded by grassroots supporters like you because I'm not running to represent corporate interests.
I'm running for Congress to represent the small business owner in Grass Valley, the working mom in Auburn, and the young adult trying to build a future in Rancho Cordova.
Over the years, I've seen what people can do when they band together, and if we're going to elect a leader who will stand up to corporate interests, fight back against Donald Trump, and challenge the establishment, then we need to be on the same page.
Friend, we're still $4,991 away from reaching our goal before the numbers go public in a few days. We **need** to hit this if we're going to have the resources to properly scale up this campaign. Will you please donate $5, $15, $35, or any amount that you can to help us reach our End of Quarter Fundraising Goal? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20260331_em_fr_b1_HH_BIG]

Heidi Hall has spent her three-decade public service career working with others to solve problems, protect our land and water, improve health, and build opportunities for others, all while raising two boys primarily as a single mom.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20260331_em_fr_b1_HH_BIG [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hall-email?refcode=20260331_em_fr_b1_HH_BIG]
Raised by parents who had persisted to make a middle-class life for their kids in Contra Costa County while lifting up others, Heidi was taught to push through and overcome challenges rather than complain about them. She learned to stick up for the vulnerable, to respect working people, and to value equal opportunity and justice.
After graduating from Pomona College and earning graduate degrees from Columbia and Rutgers, Heidi went to work for the Rockefeller Foundation promoting reproductive care and then began her career at the Environmental Protection Agency, stopping the dumping of toxic waste and holding corporate polluters accountable.
Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

# TUESDAY, March 31, 2026
---
**Dear _Texas Flyover_ Reader,** Today's sponsor is the [Texas State Historical Association](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJys0EFu6yAQxvHTwC4WAzjAgsXbZJe37dLCzDhGInYEUye9fdVKlXqAHuD36dP_7TpdU6llu_1Pd4r8WvYJCUtOTDht9OyVmKlNnelRtl6QeCWmV-qNjr2-86SVPp-UORn4JUFinBUGkBTBORu8AjByjXnxACqpecnOOpyD9eiWEMyoZosGZYlfg8oYAK9ghEHr7LMeYQ7JuzBmYRVh4b0NP0-W-rEf1Ia832WNK_OjC_NP6IvQF341OgbuaxrooI270BfZIj6epdbSz05YdbunUr81_2WBI-rPAAAA__8Pk3ah), which is hosting an event that caught our attention. If you're interested in Texas history, it's worth a look: an immersive weekend in San Antonio that goes far beyond a typical tour and brings the story of the Texas Revolution to life. -Cole, CEO
* * *

body:
In each of these 26 states, the results from these Secretary of State elections will determine not just who holds those offices but how future elections are run and the shape of our democracy as a whole.
We must make sure that pro-voter, pro-democracy, anti-suppression candidates win everywhere we can. RUSH $35 or more right now to give us the resources we need to push all year to register and turn out every eligible voter >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=033126_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
These types of elections always fly under the media's radar, Team, but this year 26 Secretary of State races will shape the future of our elections, redistricting in 2030, and the outcome of the 2028 presidential race.
Opponents of voting rights already know this, which is why they’re already pouring money into these elections – and we have to fight back now, while it still makes a difference. Check out this map:
Map of Key Secretary of State Races for 2026 [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=033126_2&amount=25]
The work to increase voter participation and turnout for these races has to start now, not this summer. We have to build the infrastructure to defend pro-voter initiatives in Arizona, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Nevada, at the same time as we work to flip the script in key battleground states like Georgia, Ohio, and Iowa.
Team: None of it happens without your support. Fuel our work for this year's elections with $35 or whatever you can today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=033126_2&amount=35]
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=033126_2&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=033126_2&amount=25]

Opponents of voting rights have been working on these objectives for years. They've targeted state legislatures and key statewide offices to control the rules around voting and that's why they've been in a position to follow up on the "Big Lie" with bill after bill suppressing the vote. They've played the long game to pick and choose their voters and protect their own power.
Most people don't know that their Secretary of State is the state official who runs their elections, let alone who the current office-holder in their state is. But they are the last line of defense against voter suppression and diminished ballot access , which is why we need to invest in voter information, registration, and participation in these critical races.
2025 was a tough year, but we did not back down. Our right to vote is too important and too much is at stake for our democracy, our fellow Americans, and the direction of our country. Driving pro-voting rights voters to the polls in November is the best possible response to all that we've been forced to live through the last decade.
Your gift -- $10, $20, $35, or more -- helps provide the resources we need to keep voters apprised of what is at stake and get them out to vote for pro-democracy policies. Please, chip in what you can today! >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=033126_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=033126_2&amount=20]

| Friends,

We are building real momentum across Georgia's First District. People are paying attention. They are responding to our message. They are ready for new leadership that will go to Washington and fight to deliver the America First agenda.
But momentum alone does not win elections. Action does. In these final hours, we need to show undeniable strength. We need to show that this campaign has the support, the energy, and the determination to win.

Joining me is Merle Meyers Boeing Whistleblower and now grief counselor. Listen in to hear about Merle's rite of passage that he went through as a 30 year, Boeing employee become whistle blower who faced blowback from the company he worked 30 years for and how he uses his experience to help others. This is a riveting story about a brave man who saw something wrong and spoke up.
Merle and his wife operate Grief and Trauma Chaplaincy (GTC). GTC is operated by Senior Chaplains Merle and Cindy Meyers. GTC provides support to help those grieving and hurting through the loss of loved ones or other life losses, and caring for those living through a traumatic event. As their tag line says: "Traumatic grief is not a disorder, it is a rite of passage." For more about Merle and the work he and his wife do visit
https://www.griefandtraumachaplaincy.com/

And today is the end of the fundraising quarter.

name: Aria, United We Dream
subject: Supreme Court hearing arguments on birthright citizenship tomorrow
body:
Birthright citizenship is under attack. | | | Peter,
For more than 150 years, the 14th Amendment has provided a simple rule: If you are born in the U.S., you are a citizen. **That right is under attack.** Tomorrow, April 1, the Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on birthright citizenship — a high-stakes case that could determine whether this fundamental constitutional right is protected. **For over 150 years, the rule has been simple.** If you are born in the United States, you are a citizen regardless of the color of your skin, religion, or your parents’ circumstances. Birthright citizenship has enabled generations of children to pursue their dreams and build a stronger country. This decision will lay out whether the administration can end the 14th Amendment and strip citizenship from millions of people born in the U.S. to immigrant parents. It hits hardest for people already struggling to get by — the working families who power our country, for whom citizenship means access to work, health care, schools, social services, and housing. The efforts to end birthright citizenship are deliberate. **If they can control who “gets to be American,” then they create a permanent underclass of everyone else.** Once a president can rewrite who is and isn’t a citizen by executive order, no one's status is truly secure — and right now, it’s our job to ensure that birthright citizenship remains intact. clean_body: Birthright citizenship is under attack. | | | Peter, For more than 150 years, the 14th Amendment has provided a simple rule: If you are born in the U.S., you are a citizen. That right is under attack. Tomorrow, April 1, the Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on birthright citizenship — a high-stakes case that could determine whether this fundamental constitutional right is protected. For over 150 years, the rule has been simple. If you are born in the United States, you are a citizen regardless of the color of your skin, religion, or your parents’ circumstances. Birthright citizenship has enabled generations of children to pursue their dreams and build a stronger country. This decision will lay out whether the administration can end the 14th Amendment and strip citizenship from millions of people born in the U.S. to immigrant parents. It hits hardest for people already struggling to get by — the working families who power our country, for whom citizenship means access to work, health care, schools, social services, and housing. The efforts to end birthright citizenship are deliberate. If they can control who “gets to be American,” then they create a permanent underclass of everyone else. Once a president can rewrite who is and isn’t a citizen by executive order, no one's status is truly secure — and right now, it’s our job to ensure that birthright citizenship remains intact. I grew up in poverty, became a teenage mom at 17, but I chose life, worked hard, graduated college while raising my daughter, and built a successful remodeling business right here in Charles County with my husband Rob.

# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128472133/611445468/-1429052514?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjU1NGRiZTItMzMyZC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=9fKNa6eStsutH5u5lb__oXM0EF49fHWa7C4bbT-m3pI=)
Hey folks, it’s Mark Kelly.

Seven years ago, I was making a decision about whether I was going to run for the Senate.

I knew it would be a lot of work. A lot of time away from home. A lot of time away from family. I knew it wouldn’t be easy.

But after two years of Donald Trump and a Republican-held Senate doing just about everything he wanted, I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines. I had to do something.

So, I ran. And, somehow, we won. And then we had to turn around and run all over again to win a full term after that. But thanks to your support, we won that one, too.

I’m grateful every day that I get to wake up, walk out the door, and defend our people, our democracy, and our Constitution. It’s one of the greatest honors of my life. And I’ve never forgotten that I wouldn’t be here without your help.

I know we’ve been in some tough fights before, but this one is different. With elections coming this November, the stakes are higher than they have ever been. The fate of our democracy hangs in the balance.

After everything that’s already happened, I wish I didn’t have to ask you for more. But that’s what I need to do.

subject: The Mountain Minute: 3/31/2026
body:
Colorado collected $3.1 billion in marijuana taxes. Here’s how much actually reaches schools.
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). And also, check out our [deep-dive video of the day](https://link.email.joinrmv.) on where Colorado's marijuana tax revenue is _actually_ going.
Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are grappling with a roughly $1.5 billion deficit, as Medicaid spending is [set to jump $2.3 BILLION](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and [progressives blame TABOR](https://link.email.joinrmv.) while pushing tax credits. At the same time, Gov. Jared Polis is [pushing plans to open or build a new prison](https://link.email.joinrmv.) to address projected inmate growth, a proposal drawing scrutiny as the state weighs cuts and competing budget priorities.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** A former Teacher of the Year finalist was [sentenced to 14 years in a child abuse case](https://link.email.joinrmv.), while delays at Xcel’s Comanche 3 plant have created a [potential summer power shortfall](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Marijuana tax revenues—[over $3.1 billion since legalization](https://link.email.joinrmv.)—are contributing only a limited share to schools, and [concerns are growing about Denver’s economy](https://link.email.joinrmv.) amid restaurant closures, falling property values, and suburban migration. Separately, a state lawmaker is calling for [greater citizen involvement in politics](https://link.email.joinrmv.), arguing grassroots participation is key to accountability.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Senate Democrats [blocked a voter ID amendment](https://link.email.joinrmv.) to the SAVE Act despite earlier support, while the Trump administration is launching a crackdown on an [estimated $250 billion in annual federal fraud](https://link.email.joinrmv.), including suspending providers and cutting questionable Medicaid payments.
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, March 31, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado collected $3.1 billion in marijuana taxes. Here’s how much actually reaches schools.](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
When Colorado voters said yes to legal marijuana back in 2012, schools were a big part of the pitch. More than a decade in, the state has collected over 3.1 billion dollars in tax revenue. So where does it all go?
That number still carries a certain weight. It suggests a level of impact that would be visible in classrooms across the state.
But when the dollars are traced through the system, then stacked up against what it actually costs to run schools, the effect looks different. Not invisible. Just smaller than people tend to expect.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**[Denver in Decline](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY TOM ANTHONY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Sharp decline in Denver businesses and real estate values:** Restaurant licenses in Denver dropped from 4,130 in 2023 to 1,780 in 2025—a roughly 57% decline—while commercial properties have lost significant value, with some buildings selling at steep discounts compared to prior valuations.
* **Economic shift toward suburbs and remote work impacts city core:** The article points to increased suburban migration, remote work trends, and reduced in-person commerce contributing to declining downtown activity, vacant storefronts, and shifting consumer patterns.
* **Criticism of policy decisions and long-term trajectory:** The piece argues that pandemic-era policies, rising taxes, and government interventions have contributed to economic strain and population shifts, raising broader concerns about Denver’s long-term economic direction.

**[Self-Governance Is Not a Spectator Sport](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY REP. KEN DEGRAAF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Lawmakers argue participation is key to representation:** The commentary contends that meaningful representation requires active citizen involvement—including time, attention, and financial support—rather than relying solely on voting.
* **Political influence tied to funding and engagement:** The piece emphasizes that campaigns are shaped by money and participation, arguing that broader grassroots contributions can counterbalance large, concentrated donors and increase accountability.
* **Calls for increased citizen involvement in governance:** The author urges voters to take a more active role in supporting candidates aligned with their values, warning that disengagement leads to greater government expansion and reduced accountability.

subject: Farm workers are the backbone of this country

body:
---
| | Peter,

This year, we are reminded more than ever that the decades-long fight for workers’ rights and dignity on the job has never been about just one person.

I am heartbroken for the women who have come forward to share their experiences of abuse, and I commend them for their courage. I’m also thinking about everyone in the labor movement who has been impacted by this news.

But the work to protect workers – especially those who have too often been overlooked – must continue.

Here in California, farm workers have long done some of the hardest and most essential work in our economy, often under difficult and dangerous conditions. Their contributions help feed our communities and sustain our state, and they deserve fair pay, safe workplaces, and the ability to speak up without fear.

**The fight for basic worker protections has always been bigger than any one individual. It’s about making sure every worker is treated with dignity and respect.**

I remain committed to advancing that work in Congress – strengthening health and safety protections, supporting fair wages, and ensuring workers can organize to improve their conditions.

Thank you for standing with working people,

Scott

---

Peter,

I said it earlier this week, and summarizes what Democrats have been up to the last 40+ days:

_“TSA agents are not getting paid, and they are showing up to work.

Democrats are getting paid, and they are not showing up for work.”_

Hardworking TSA officers secured our airports without paychecks for weeks , while Senate Democrats collected their six-figure salaries and skipped critical work — all to make a political statement.

There are plenty of real issues where we need our government to take action right now. Like preventing a massive global conflict. Or bringing down the cost of housing and groceries. Or fixing our health care system. But instead of getting to work for the American people, Trump and his MAGA buddies have been advancing their out-of-touch agenda. Here are just a few of their recent big ideas:
* Prevent American citizens from voting by passing the “SAVE” Act to rig the midterms.
* Ask Congress for $200 billion — and even charge Americans a new 8% fee for sending mail with the USPS — pay for his illegal war in Iran.
* Put Trump’s face on a 24K gold coin and add his signature to paper currencies — while families struggle every day to afford groceries and gas.
* Refuse to fund TSA and unleash chaos in our airports so that ICE can continue terrorizing our communities.
* Build a $400 million, gold-encrusted White House ballroom into a corruption magnet — where billionaires and corporations can buy anonymous access.

**I’ve got four words for them: Not on my watch.** I’m fighting back against MAGA Republicans to put a stop to this unprecedented corruption, protect our basic freedoms, and put our government on the side of working people, not the rich and powerful. **And before tonight’s FEC fundraising deadline, I want to ask if you can pitch in to support our campaign. Why? Because the special interests we’re fighting against will dig into our public fundraising report to evaluate the strength of our campaign. This is our chance to prove that their agenda is extremely unpopular — and there’s a strong grassroots movement fighting to stop them.** [**If it makes sense for you right now, can you chip in $28 or any amount before midnight tonight to power this movement, fight back against the GOP’s extremist agenda, and make our government work for working people?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3565?amount=28&t=8&akid=2839%2E4032634%2EsF83av)

_**EXHIBIT 1 - JOINT FUNDRAISING NOTICE **_

Team Nunn ("JFC") is a joint fundraising committee composed of Iowans for Zach Nunn ("Campaign"), Call to Service PAC ("LPAC") and NRCC (each, a "Committee," and, collectively, the "Committees"). Any contribution to the JFC permissible under the Federal Election Campaign Act, as amended ("FECA"), from contributors who have not exceeded their applicable federal contribution limits, shall be allocated among the Committees pursuant to FECA and the formula set forth in this Notice.

_**Contributions Made by an Individual or Federal Non-Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Individuals or federal non-multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $322,100. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $7,000, designating up to $3,500 to the primary election and up to $3,500 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3\. NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $44,300 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

_**Contributions Made by a Federal Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $120,000. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $10,000, designating up to $5,000 to the primary election and up to $5,000 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3 .NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $15,000 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5 .NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

Contributions to Team Nunn, or to any participating Committee individually, are not deductible as charitable donations for federal income tax purposes. Contributions from corporations, labor organizations, national banks, federal government contractors, foreign nationals without green cards, and other federally impermissible sources are prohibited. The contributor's signature designates his or her contribution to the elections described above. Contributions that exceed a donor's contribution limit to a participating Committee shall be reallocated to the remaining Committees according to this allocation formula to the extent permitted by FECA. Any contributor may designate his or her contribution to a specific participant Committee to the extent permitted by FECA. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, mailing address, occupation, and name of employer of each individual whose aggregate contributions exceed $200 in an election cycle or calendar year, as applicable.

The contrast in this race is becoming a clear choice between two very different paths. _Republicans have already lined up two opponents to try and drift Rhode Island towards extremism._

[ ]( Peter, when I walk into Team Jena campaign headquarters on Monday mornings, I never know what might be waiting on my desk. Yesterday, I walked into this: [ ]( Jena's campaign for Congress is running on all cylinders. But between Jena’s packed Town Hall earlier this month, our voter meet-and-greets last week, and another strong weekend of door-knocking, our team is almost out of, well, almost everything. I won’t sugarcoat it, Peter, running out of critical materials like campaign flyers is a big problem. It’s also a big sign. Every Post-it note taped to my desk yesterday means that Jena and our volunteers are reaching OK-05 voters at an unprecedented pace. People in our district aren’t just hearing Jena’s message, they’re onboard. Heck, apparently another 100 folks or so will be sporting our newest T-shirt! → Don’t wait for HQ to restock! [Grab your Jena for Congress tee at the Team Jena store]( and our union shop will ship one straight to your door! Still, Peter, momentum only works if we have the tools to support it. Seeing those post-it notes, it was clear: We urgently needed to place another round of orders with our printer, our T-shirt vendor, and our button supplier. If we don’t keep materials in volunteers’ hands, we risk slowing down just when things are accelerating. So I took a risk. ### The Quinceañera Counterpunch Heard 'Round the Valley
Let's start with the moment that put this campaign on the national radar.
Shortly after Bobby won the primary, Congresswoman Monica de la Cruz went on the attack, attempting to dismiss him as a celebrity who "just does quinceañeras." But what was meant as an easy layup instead, became one of the most spectacular own goals of the 2026 cycle.
Bobby's campaign didn't flinch. They didn't huddle for two weeks with consultants and focus groups. They leaned in and publicly embraced the quinceañera as exactly what it is: a sacred rite of passage in Latino culture, a celebration of family, faith, and community. Bobby announced he'd be honored to attend quinceañeras across the district. See his video response below:
[](https://substack..xg_gZPPAd3HKSKDfV8LffTym06r0fGYQ04GcWuhNDqM?/#tiktok-iframe?media=1&app=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tiktok.com%2F%40bobbypulidofortexas%2Fvideo%2F7615788934605376782&key=e27c740634285c9ddc20db64f73358dd)
[@bobbypulidofortexas](https://substack.com/redirect/0b373dac-1c1a-4b92-bb54-ac380da816b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)[My opponent said I only belong playing at quinceañeras. I'll take that as a compliment. Quinceañeras are about family, tradition, and community. That's exactly what this campaign is about. Got one coming up in District 15? Send us a DM. I'd be honored to stop by.](https://substack..xg_gZPPAd3HKSKDfV8LffTym06r0fGYQ04GcWuhNDqM?/#tiktok-iframe?media=1&app=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tiktok.com%2F%40bobbypulidofortexas%2Fvideo%2F7615788934605376782&key=e27c740634285c9ddc20db64f73358dd)
The result? Over 2,000 requests from constituents, and counting.
"The more people you talk to out on the ground and they see what you're about," Bobby told us, "it inoculates you from all that negativity they throw your way."
As Mike Madrid put it on the show: when they go negative, that's the best day of the campaign. It means the momentum is yours and they have nothing left but to try to tear you down.
* * *
### Swift and Real Responses to ICE Detainments
If the quinceañera story showed the campaign's cultural instincts, his response to ICE's detainment of the Mariachi teens showed his campaign's speed.
When the Gamez-Cuellar boys were detained by immigration authorities, Bobby got word on a plane back from New York. He landed, got in an Uber, pulled out his phone, and recorded a video calling out ICE and the Congresswoman on a Saturday afternoon.
He didn't ask for permission. He didn't schedule a press conference. He didn't wait for a poll.
Within days, Monica de la Cruz had set up a podium and was publicly parading the detained teenager out of the facility, a remarkable reversal for a Republican who had campaigned on mass deportations just over a year ago.
The lesson for campaigns everywhere: instincts matter. Over-consulting a moment can kill it. The social media era rewards candidates who trust their gut and move in real time.
[](https://substack..xg_gZPPAd3HKSKDfV8LffTym06r0fGYQ04GcWuhNDqM?/#tiktok-iframe?media=1&app=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tiktok.com%2F%40bobbypulidofortexas%2Fvideo%2F7614604538028346638&key=e27c740634285c9ddc20db64f73358dd)
[@bobbypulidofortexas](https://substack.com/redirect/0b373dac-1c1a-4b92-bb54-ac380da816b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)[These Mariachi students from McAllen were good enough for Monica De La Cruz's photo ops. Now they're in detention centers and she's nowhere to be found. South Texas notices.](https://substack..xg_gZPPAd3HKSKDfV8LffTym06r0fGYQ04GcWuhNDqM?/#tiktok-iframe?media=1&app=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tiktok.com%2F%40bobbypulidofortexas%2Fvideo%2F7614604538028346638&key=e27c740634285c9ddc20db64f73358dd)
* * *
### "God, Family, and Country." Bobby is not Your Usual Democrat
Bobby was remarkably candid about where his own party has lost the plot with Latino voters, and it's worth sitting with what he said.
"Democratic politicians got away from the family structure," he told us. "We let the Republican party literally run on God, family, and country. And those things in the Hispanic culture resonate."
He's not wrong. For a generation, Republicans were the only side to fully voice those values. The result? A historic shift in Latino voting patterns in 2024 that Democrats are still trying to understand.
Bobby describes himself as a conservative Democrat. Someone who believes in community, in the social contract, in workers having a shot. But someone who also embraces the values of faith and family that are central to Latino life. He doesn't think that's an oxymoron. He thinks it's a roadmap.
He's also clear-eyed about the party's problem with young Latino men, who increasingly feel that Democrats don't speak to their values or their identity. His solution isn't to abandon progressive priorities. It's to speak the language of provider, protector, and community builder that young men in the Valley actually recognize.
"We're so unbalanced politically right now," he said. "The Republican party is very male dominated and the Democratic party is very female dominated. I'm a Democrat man running against a Republican woman. That's going to be an interesting dynamic."
* * *
### What's at Stake
TX-15 is a Trump-leaning district in the Rio Grande Valley: a heavily Latino region that has seen some of the most significant political shifts of the past four years. But the data across the Southwest is showing double-digit point Latino swing back toward Democrats, and Bobby Pulido is running directly into that wave.
This is the kind of race that defines what the next chapter of the Democratic Party looks like in Latino America. Not a party that talks at Latinos, but one that reflects them, their faith, their families, their work ethic, their pride.
"Anybody that can unite the Latino vote will unite the country," Bobby said as we wrapped up. "I honestly believe that. We hold the key. We are the future. And any party that neglects us, neglects us at their peril."

name: Christopher Ahuja for Congress
subject: Sherman v. Sanders: History proves the case.
body:
Brad Sherman is more of the same that we can’t afford

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=d175b41cc6&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,
This weekend, thousands of U.S. Marines were deployed to the Middle East as tensions with Iran escalate.We have seen this pattern before. Escalation first, accountability later—if it comes at all. The Constitution is clear that Congress decides when we go to war, yet leaders in Washington keep sidestepping that responsibility while the consequences grow.This isn’t new. We’ve seen this before.**In October of 2001, Congress rushed to pass H.R.3162** –The Patriot Act–in a moment of fear, expanding federal power and helping lay the groundwork for DHS and ICE.**Brad Sherman voted yes.****Bernie Sanders voted no.****That difference matters.** Because Congress never seems to hesitate when it comes to funding war abroad, including blank-check support for Israel’s military actions. The money moves quickly for weapons and escalation. When it comes to healthcare, housing, or lowering costs here at home, those same leaders suddenly talk about limits.**Brad Sherman has been part of that for decades.** That is not leadership. That is complicity.I am running for Congress to change that. I will fight to reassert Congress’s authority over war powers and stop writing checks for wars the public never voted for, while families here at home are told to wait.[**We are closing out this fundraising quarter tonight. If you want representation that will actually draw a line, I am asking you to help us get there before midnight.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=ced8e8ff7f&e=53c7d12fc7)

subject: What it looks like when your state has a Democratic governor
body:

Wes Moore is spending this year’s legislative session focused on kitchen table issues: Work, wages, and wealth.
What does that look like? Working with the General Assembly, the Governor’s fighting for relief from skyrocketing utility costs for Marylanders. He’s attracting new businesses and jobs to our state. He’s making historic investments in education, and making sure people feel safe in their communities.
That’s what states with Democratic governors look like. And even though we can’t count on anything but chaos coming out of Washington with Trump’s reckless agenda, we can count on Democratic governors to fight back.

In times like these, I know it can feel like small, individual actions can’t make a difference. That the politicians running the show in DC are too powerful, too isolated for any single person to make a difference. But that’s not true at all, Derek.
**And Pennsylvania would know.**
250 years ago, a group of Americans gathered in Philadelphia to declare its independence from the most powerful empire in the world. Just a small handful of people had the courage to tell the entire world that we had the power to determine America’s future. **Not a king. Not a tyrant.**
I think about that story a lot, Derek. Because I see so many parallels between then and now.
I see how small, individual actions — the decision to join a campaign, the courage to protest peacefully, the bravery to speak out against injustice — have added up and changed Pennsylvania for the better.
[_**That’s what this campaign is all about. Small, but significant actions all coming together into something bigger. Something unstoppable. Now, I’m asking you to join me — to take that small step and help us build a brighter future for Pennsylvania. Wake up, Virginia! Share this message! Virginians are voting right now on whether to allow far left politicians to redraw Virginia's congressional maps. What’s the difference between Yes and No? A "yes" means Rural Virginia will be silenced and represented by far left Fairfax politicians. A "yes" means Virginians will be taxed so that illegal immigrants can get free stuff. A "yes" will send the very SAME democrats who are disarming and overtaxing us in Virginia to represent us in Washington. We cannot allow that!! Democrats call this temporary, which is what politicians always say when they want to justify taking more of your money and power. It’s a lie. There is nothing temporary about the outcome and power they seek. Democrats want a permanently blue Virginia and your apathy or inaction will give them that. You can do nothing and suffer the consequences, oryou can vote NO and rejectsocialist politicians silencing dissent in Virginia. Vote early at your county election office or on April 21st at your usual precinct. Save RURAL Virginia byvoting NO!
|

Why the FEC deadline tonight means more than a number on a spreadsheet

| |
---|---|---
| | | Forwarded this email? [Subscribe here](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oYWxleWZvcm1pLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.6h4fIS8yxwRvdPder44lq-HvPSTX0dXK6t7pB9yg_r4?) for more

# [This is about more than a deadline](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=192755469&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkyNzU1NDY5LCJpYXQiOjE3NzQ5ODgxOTUsImV4cCI6MTc3NzU4MDE5NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.o3rusBziRQQFSETKMLoq2lr8WlPkA6zmtZ5Qun6LwSU)
### Why the FEC deadline tonight means more than a number on a spreadsheet
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Mar 31
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL3RoaXMtaXMtYWJvdXQtbW9yZS10aGFuLWEtZGVhZGxpbmU_.YsuwQaTTNXx9OqfUcypOlEGdOdxLlkTvXcY6u8XcZbQ?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/this-is-about-more-than-a-deadline?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

**I need to be honest.**
I just got out of a finance meeting about tonight's FEC deadline, and it wasn't great.
I want you to hear the hard truth from me: We set a **$500,000 end-of-quarter goal** , and we're behind where we need to be.
**[We need to see a surge of donations before midnight to close the gap.](https://substack.com/redirect/4db330ac-2710-4397-b174-a4cb2e4e123b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And I'm not going to pretend this FEC deadline is some insider political metric that only matters to people who spend their days staring at campaign spreadsheets.
It matters.
_A lot._
Because after this end-of-quarter deadline hits, **[the FEC will make our fundraising numbers public.](https://substack.com/redirect/4db330ac-2710-4397-b174-a4cb2e4e123b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
That means the media sees them. National Republicans see them. MAGA megadonors see them. And the people deciding whether to invest in this race - _or attack us even harder_ - see them too.
So no, this is not just about balancing a spreadsheet. **It 's about showing strength in one of the most important Senate races in the country.**
And at the end of the day, truly, behind the numbers and the campaign and everything else: It's about whether working families in Michigan have a fighter in their corner in the U.S. Senate - or whether this seat gets handed over to a MAGA Republican backed by out-of-state billionaires and Donald Trump.
Those are the real stakes here.
I'm running for Senate to serve Michiganders. To fight for the folks I know who work hard, play by the rules, and still feel like the system is leaving them behind.
I'm fighting for workers, families, farmers, teachers, nurses, and small-business owners who deserve a government that actually sees them and makes their lives better.
And I think people can sense that when they meet me. They can tell I mean it.
That may be one reason I'm leading in the polls, and why I'm the Democrat with the best shot to defeat Republican Mike Rogers.
**But I need to be real with you: I 'm not wealthy. Unlike my opponents, I'm not a millionaire. I don't have a shady network of rich friends writing checks to buy a Senate seat.**
But that's what we're up against.
We already know Mike Rogers is backed by a Texas oil billionaire who poured $5 million into Michigan. And now the Koch network is gearing up to dump dark money into this race, too.
That's because national Republicans see Michigan as one of their best chances to grow their Senate majority.
They are not messing around. _We can 't either._
That's why I need you to stand with me today.
**You are the power of this movement** - the grassroots supporters who care deeply about their communities and their country.
The people who are willing to say, _I 'm in._
Whether that's $5, $20, or whatever you can manage, it all adds up. It all shows the strength behind this campaign.
**[If you're in a position to chip in today, I'm asking you directly: Help us close this gap before midnight. Help us show the strength of this campaign. Help us prove that Michigan is not for sale.](https://substack.com/redirect/4db330ac-2710-4397-b174-a4cb2e4e123b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/4db330ac-2710-4397-b174-a4cb2e4e123b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/4db330ac-2710-4397-b174-a4cb2e4e123b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

the Supreme Court will hear arguments on whether Trump can dismantle the
14th Amendment and decide who gets to be an American.

This is an all-out assault on the Constitution — and it’s happening
because we’re facing a captured, loyalist-packed Court that has already
shown it’s willing to do Trump’s bidding.

Lower courts have made this clear: Trump’s order to end birthright
citizenship is unconstitutional. But he’s not backing down.

He’s asking the Court to overrule more than a century of settled law and
gut one of our most fundamental rights.

And the playbook is as extreme as it gets.

Trump’s lawyers are reviving legal theories rooted in racism, xenophobia,
and white supremacist ideology — arguments once used to deny citizenship
and equality to Black Americans and immigrants — as the foundation for his
case.

If this Court goes along with it, the consequences will be immediate.
Birthright citizenship could be effectively ended. The 14th Amendment
hollowed out. And Trump will be empowered to weaponize the Court to push
an even more extreme, unconstitutional agenda.

This is what court capture looks like.

subject: A little slice of comfort from my kitchen 🌶️

body:
After a long day in Congress, making a delicious meal has always been a way to reset and keep me grounded.
#
Peter,
I don’t know about you, but when the political noise gets a little too loud, I find myself gravitating toward the kitchen. Something about slowing down to chop veggies, smelling the wafting flavors mix together, and having a quiet moment over the stove is truly grounding.
For me, cooking has always been a way to reset. After a long day in Congress, making a meal reminds me of why we do this work in the first place — **to care for our neighbors and create something beautiful out of that care.**
Lately, I’ve been making a new recipe that has quickly become a favorite comfort dish: **Roasted Peppers Vegetarian Tamale Pie**. It’s warm, hearty, packed with flavor, and perfect for feeding a crowd (or for leftovers after a long day of fighting for our democracy).
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260331-1.cOSEoV&refcode=em20260331-6077&t=1&akid=6077%2E420207%2EwMo_s0)
[**So, I wanted to do something special today. Our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline is here, and we need to hit our $40,000 goal before midnight. For anyone who pitches in to help us reach it, I’ll send along my Roasted Peppers Vegetarian Tamale Pie recipe with your donation receipt. A small thank you from my kitchen to yours!**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260331-1.cOSEoV&refcode=em20260331-6077&amount=3&t=2&akid=6077%2E420207%2EwMo_s0)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260331-1.cOSEoV&amount=3&refcode=em20260331-6077&t=21&akid=6077%2E420207%2EwMo_s0)**
Whether you’re fueling up before knocking on doors, unwinding after work, or gathering your family around the table – I hope this dish brings you comfort and reminds you that you’re a part of a community that cares deeply about each other.
And if you end up making it, please let me know how this recipe turns out for you! I’d love to hear from you and see your creations.
With gratitude (and a warm piece of tamale pie),
Pramila Jayapal

clean_body: After a long day in Congress, making a delicious meal has always been a way to reset and keep me grounded. Peter, I don’t know about you, but when the political noise gets a little too loud, I find myself gravitating toward the kitchen. Something about slowing down to chop veggies, smelling the wafting flavors mix together, and having a quiet moment over the stove is truly grounding. For me, cooking has always been a way to reset. After a long day in Congress, making a meal reminds me of why we do this work in the first place — to care for our neighbors and create something beautiful out of that care. Lately, I’ve been making a new recipe that has quickly become a favorite comfort dish: Roasted Peppers Vegetarian Tamale Pie. It’s warm, hearty, packed with flavor, and perfect for feeding a crowd (or for leftovers after a long day of fighting for our democracy). Whether you’re fueling up before knocking on doors, unwinding after work, or gathering your family around the table – I hope this dish brings you comfort and reminds you that you’re a part of a community that cares deeply about each other. And if you end up making it, please let me know how this recipe turns out for you! I’d love to hear from you and see your creations. With gratitude (and a warm piece of tamale pie), Pramila Jayapal | | Email us: info@pramilaforcongress.com

body:
🚨 FINAL DAY — FEC Deadline Tonight at Midnight
This is it. Midnight tonight.
Our first FEC number goes public. A strong report changes this race. Will you be counted?
Friend,
I'll keep this short. You've heard from me this week and I respect your time.
Tonight at midnight, our first FEC fundraising report closes. The number we file is public. It will be scrutinized by our opponents, by national political committees, and by every reporter covering this race.
**A strong number says:** Southwest Washington is ready for new leadership. A candidate with real experience, in the Navy, in business, and in the Legislature, has the backing to win a toss-up race.
**A weak number says:** Maybe this district is content with an incumbent who votes with D.C. leadership on border security, parental rights, and fiscal discipline.
I'm not asking for a fortune. I'm asking you to be counted. **$25 before midnight** is a statement. It says you believe Southwest Washington can do better and you're willing to invest in it.
[Make It Count — Donate Now ](https://votebraun.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=18b5086f5b76ceb7f0a23578b&id=44c34cbb82&e=90b300faf9)
Thank you for everything. Win or lose tonight's fundraising goal, I'm in this race because our communities deserve better. But your support right now makes the road ahead a whole lot clearer.
John Braun
Candidate for Congress, WA-03
Captain, USN (Ret.) • President, Braun Northwest

A few days ago, I shared a little about my first and only FEC fundraising deadline of this campaign. **That deadline is at midnight tonight.**
Before I get into the technical details of it all, I want to talk a bit more about my story and why I'm running.
As a Capitol Police Officer and as an American, January 6th, 2021, was the darkest day of my life. I was immersed for what felt like countless hours in a profane mix of sweat, screams, shrieks, anger, death, fear, blood, broken limbs, spit, hatred, horror, racism, and bigotry.
The wounds that my heroic fellow officers endured are still healing. But my commitment to ensuring the strength of our democracy has only deepened.
**It 's the reason I'm running for Congress in Maryland's 5th District.**
I made this choice because I cannot sit idly by while our very right to survive is under attack by Donald Trump. I've fought against his angry mob before, and I'm ready to do it again.
So I'm asking you to make a choice:
* Either we sit back, let the bigots win, and allow corporate PACs to buy this seat out from under us.
* Or we can step up and prove we won't surrender in the face of hate.

But campaigns aren't won overnight -- they are won dollar by dollar, week by week.
Right now, weeks into this campaign, the most critical way everyone can step up is by pitching in toward my 105,000 donor goal. If we hit each and every fundraising milestone, we can afford the resources necessary to win this race and flip the House.
Look, I know you're probably tired of hearing about it, and I promise it's the last time I'll ask. But we're still short and we're counting on grassroots supporters to bridge the gap.
#### **[I'm not a millionaire. There's no turning back if we don't hit our first and ONLY FEC goal, so I'm asking you personally: Will you step up right now with a donation of any amount? Your urgent support before 11:59 p.m. could put us over the top:](https://substack.com/redirect/cbf3b06d-0ec9-43ef-9bb2-748525c1d40a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN](https://substack.com/redirect/cbf3b06d-0ec9-43ef-9bb2-748525c1d40a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The election analysts, the TV pundits, and Republicans frothing at the mouth to undermine my campaign will be looking very closely when we report our numbers.
**If we don 't hit our fundraising milestones, GOP mega-donors will see our campaign as weak and flood this race with MILLIONS to undermine us.**
Our democracy can't afford another two years of Trump's MAGA House majority. The American people can't either.
#### **[That's why I am counting on you to give whatever you can right now. Please, before 11:59 p.m., rush in any amount you can to be one of the grassroots supporters we need to get us across the finish line, win this race, and flip the House:](https://substack.com/redirect/cbf3b06d-0ec9-43ef-9bb2-748525c1d40a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you 💙
Harry

That deadline is at midnight tonight. Before I get into the technical details of it all, I want to talk a bit more about my story and why I'm running. As a Capitol Police Officer and as an American, January 6th, 2021, was the darkest day of my life. I was immersed for what felt like countless hours in a profane mix of sweat, screams, shrieks, anger, death, fear, blood, broken limbs, spit, hatred, horror, racism, and bigotry. The wounds that my heroic fellow officers endured are still healing. But my commitment to ensuring the strength of our democracy has only deepened. It 's the reason I'm running for Congress in Maryland's 5th District. I made this choice because I cannot sit idly by while our very right to survive is under attack by Donald Trump. I've fought against his angry mob before, and I'm ready to do it again. So I'm asking you to make a choice: Either we sit back, let the bigots win, and allow corporate PACs to buy this seat out from under us. Or we can step up and prove we won't surrender in the face of hate. But campaigns aren't won overnight -- they are won dollar by dollar, week by week. Right now, weeks into this campaign, the most critical way everyone can step up is by pitching in toward my 105,000 donor goal. If we hit each and every fundraising milestone, we can afford the resources necessary to win this race and flip the House. Look, I know you're probably tired of hearing about it, and I promise it's the last time I'll ask. But we're still short and we're counting on grassroots supporters to bridge the gap. The election analysts, the TV pundits, and Republicans frothing at the mouth to undermine my campaign will be looking very closely when we report our numbers. If we don 't hit our fundraising milestones, GOP mega-donors will see our campaign as weak and flood this race with MILLIONS to undermine us. * Over 7,600 people showed up again at county assemblies.
* And about 1,330 delegates attended State Assembly this past weekend, where 1,480 votes were counted.

We must keep the momentum in our fight to move to a popular vote system, even with opponents of voting rights fighting back in these two states and elsewhere across the country. From the NPVIC to other movements to advance the popular vote, we've got to keep advancing in the right direction.
We need to keep pushing forward so we can have our presidential elections come down to the popular vote -- chip in with $25 or more to stand for voting rights, democracy, and so much more >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=033126_3&amount=25]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
The movement to end the Electoral College is making progress, friend: Minnesota and Maine are just the latest states to join the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.
If you don't remember -- The National Popular Vote Interstate Compact (NPVIC) is an agreement among a group of U.S. states and the District of Columbia to award all their electoral votes to whichever presidential candidate wins the overall popular vote in the 50 states and the District of Columbia. 17 states plus DC have now joined.
Minnesota brought 10 electoral votes, and Maine 4, now accounting for 209 Electoral College votes of the 270 needed to win the election and totaling 78% of what is needed to effectively make the popular vote the law of the land. Minnesota passed a slate of voting rights protections alongside joining the compact as well, which represents huge progress.
Whether it's through the NPVIC or one of the other legal alternatives, ending the Electoral College forever is a big priority.
We are going to make this happen! Keep the momentum going and put us over the top so we can end the Electoral College forever with $25 or more today! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=033126_3&amount=25]

State legislatures in Nevada, Michigan, and more are heeding the call and also considering bills to join the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact.
The Electoral College is the biggest tool that opponents of voting rights have to swing national elections and suppress the will of the people. We have to take away this dangerous mechanism that enabled the January 6th insurrection by any means necessary.

subject: Look, I'll be the first to admit that NOTHING about this year (or the last) has been easy.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by In This Together PAC
body:
I want to speak to you directly for a minute, Peter.

This year hasn't exactly started off easy for millions of Americans. Health insurance premiums are higher. Tariffs have driven costs up across the board. And now a war in the Middle East is sending gas prices through the roof. There's a lot of noise, a lot of frustration, and frankly—a lot of folks wondering if our elected leaders are actually focused on helping them.

_But I'll tell you what I've seen: people like you stepping up anyway._

Folks who still believe that public service should be about improving lives, protecting fundamental rights, and doing the job with honesty and integrity. That's why I started In This Together PAC in the first place, Peter. **To support good people and good candidates who are ready to take on the challenges of public office to get things done.**

I am living proof that when candidates and elected officials stay focused on improving the lives of the people they work for, voters reward them at the polls—even in tough territory.

At In This Together PAC, we’re taking that lesson to red and purple states across the country, to help good candidates win. Right now, we're only hours away from our March fundraising deadline, and what we raise right now is going to help shape what we can actually get done in the months ahead.

So, if you can, chip in any amount that works for you to help my team and I keep building the momentum we need to take ten steps in the right direction come Election Day. >> [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/itt-q1-2026 &refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128485576/611475645/1338299492?refcode=em26_260331_eoq2_fndd_gq_act___GOVAB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260331_eoq2_fndd_gq_act___GOVAB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=d64e309f-452d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDY0ZTMwOWYtNDUyZC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=fMje6HDpK6d2NL49l85Tajr4i3QuMJkjuvpOYDAm1PE=)

Peter, what’s happening in Washington right now is the exact opposite of results over rhetoric. The Senate unanimously passed a bill that would end the DHS shutdown, fund TSA, Coast Guard and FEMA, and leave ICE to be debated — but Speaker Mike Johnson and House Republicans _wouldn’t even allow a vote_ on the compromise legislation. Here’s the proof that our movement is working — and winning.

Peter,
When we first started Leaders We Deserve, a lot of people were skeptical.
They thought the Democratic Party wasn’t ready for that kind of change. That young progressives couldn’t actually win. Their agendas were too radical, and the candidates were unelectable.
**They’ve never been more wrong.**
Just in the past 6 months, we’ve backed **Zohran Mamdani’s** historic victory in New York City, helped elect **Akbar Ali** , Georgia’s youngest state representative, and endorsed a slate of bold progressive fighters across the country who are reshaping the Party from the ground up.
**[I’ll tell you more about our wins, but first, can you pitch in $5 to help us hit our $100,000 end-of-quarter goal by midnight? Hitting it means we have the resources to keep backing the courageous leaders this moment demands.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260331_1_wins.IcK8pH&refcode=em20260331-3315&amount=5&t=2&akid=3315%2E587540%2EMuWRi9)**

In the first quarter of 2026 alone, we’ve shown the power of what this movement can do.
**Christian Menefee** won a congressional seat in Texas. **Demi Palecek** beat back hundreds of thousands in corporate dark money to win her Illinois primary. **Nabeela Syed** advanced to the general for an Illinois State Senate seat. And **Julio Salinas** moved to a runoff in Texas, still fighting to flip a competitive district in the Rio Grande Valley.
_That’s just three months in._
And we’re not done yet. We have **Justin J. Pearson** in Tennessee, **Donavan McKinney** in Michigan, **Patrick Roath** in Massachusetts, **Claire Valdez** in New York, and **Nate Blouin** in Utah. These are leaders who are shaking the table, challenging power, and giving the establishment a run for their money — **and that’s exactly why they’ll win.**
These candidates and the grassroots energy behind them will define what kind of Democratic Party we take into November and beyond — and how we flip the House, win back state legislatures, and build real power for working people.
And there are more primaries and endorsements on the way.
**Our end-of-quarter deadline is tonight at midnight, and we’re still $22,983 away from reaching our $100,000 goal.** We need to make sure our slate of candidates have the resources they need to win, and our movement has the momentum to carry us through November.

David Hogg

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I walked off the floor of the Texas House.
body:
This is what I learned:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
In just a minute, I’m going to personally ask you to [**make a $5 contribution to my campaign for governor before tonight’s midnight deadline.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260331_2_leap.-Uf0XZ&refcode=em20260331-848&amount=5&t=1&akid=848%2E299639%2EkSryiM)
Before I do, I hope you’ll let me share **an important lesson I’ve learned about faith**.
Back in 2021, the Texas GOP was ramming an extreme anti-voter bill through the State House. The voter suppression bill they were pushing was ugly. It was dangerous. And I knew that staying put would mean letting Texans lose their freedom to vote.
So I took a leap of faith. I chose to walk off the floor.
But I knew I couldn’t stop this bill on my own. I needed my fellow Democratic legislators with me in order to break quorum. So I stood up and I texted other legislators:
_“A leap of faith only works if you take it.”_
Together, we ran out the clock and stopped a bill designed to silence Texas voters. That quorum break protected Sunday morning voting — a sacred tradition in Black churches — and blocked a provision that would have allowed partisan judges to overturn election results without evidence. And we earned that victory together.
**Just like I needed my fellow Texas Democrats by my side on that day five years ago, I’m asking you to join me today.** I’m asking you to have faith that we can finally unseat corrupt Governor Greg Abbott and flip Texas blue together.
Each time you chip in to our people-powered campaign, you’re doing it alongside thousands of others who also believe in our power to win a brighter future for every Texan.
**[Can I count on you to donate for the very first time before tonight’s big deadline?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260331_2_leap.-Uf0XZ&refcode=em20260331-848&amount=5&t=2&akid=848%2E299639%2EkSryiM)**

_A leap of faith only works if you take it._ And when you do, others will leap with you.
No te dejes.
— Gina

| Peter,
Earlier this month, I tried to conduct oversight at a newly uncovered secret ICE facility in Frederick, Colorado.
I'm a state representative. I showed up peacefully and asked for transparency.
They wouldn't let me in.
That should worry every single one of us.
A recent investigation reveals there are multiple secretive ICE detention facilities operating across Colorado -- from Craig to Pueblo to Denver. Facilities the public barely knows about and that appear to be operating with little transparency.
Clearly, these are secretive facilities that ICE doesn't want the public to know about, operating outside of ICE's own guidelines. These "hold rooms" may have no beds and no access to legal representation or medical care, but ICE has held people as young as one year old and as old as ninety-one for weeks at a time.
So here's what we're going to do about it.
We're putting pressure on Congress to investigate these facilities and issue subpoenas if necessary to find out why they exist and what's happening inside them.
But our current representative, Gabe Evans, has refused to demand answers.
Colorado deserves better.

Th all-powerful, ancient and evil spirit of personal greed, which had only been held in check by legislation, and a popular culture that shamed anyone to openly displaying it since that fateful day the stock market crashed in of 1929.
