It's a big club... and you ain 't in it." That last line's the most oft-repeated aphorism from late comedian--and I'd argue prophet--George Carlin's 2005 HBO special, "Life Is Worth Losing." But that second to last line isn't quoted as often, and it's just as important. We've seen it with our own eyes, both in the two decades before he said it (if you were alive), and the two decades since. | | ---|---|--- I know this because...I was in this big club. Kinda. I attended their schools, went to their parties, and watched as the world began to burn and nobody could be bothered to off the couch to grab an industrial-sized extinguisher. Michael Wolff was and is in this club. And I'm so exhausted analyzing how our politics and overall culture went so seriously to crap that a court jester with piss-cotton candy for hair, congealed cheese for an IQ, and tantrums like a toddler in between girdle fittings and adult-diaper changings could be elected to run the "free world," without talking about what I saw firsthand. It's the banality of evil as lifestyle choice and accumulation of wealth and power as end goals that got us here. I was often invited to participate, though I was suspect as I attended the right institutions but grew up in a rent control apartment below 59th Street. LOL, you should've seen how my bus home from school emptied--like it'd sprung a VX gas leak, or Stephen Miller suddenly appeared to hand out dating advice--once we passed the bridge downtown on 2nd Avenue. Michael Wolff, whose babe in the woods routine collapsed once the Epstein Estate released many of the emails between the two men, could not have been any more in this club, or at least he could not have been trying any harder to stay on the right side of its gated community. A perfect product of the era that created Epstein, he was. So we're gonna talk about Wolff. And others. Some may get mad, I'm naming names. And, well, if they do, too fucking bad. They took the easy path or hedonistic one and have helped bring our country to the brink. And this is where I tell you kids out there that America wasn't always a fash-adjacent dystopia. There was a time before The Rise of the Super Predators, when America was on a similar path to Western European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan, and other high-income democracies. Yes, I did mean America. And not, say, Narnia or Wakanda (more realistic these days). If you want just an example, we often led the world in life expectancy in the 1950s and 60s. Well, here we are today in all our "America First" glory: | | ---|---|--- We didn't arrive there by accident, it was choices made by Epstein's Predator Class, from creating economic theories to enrich the already rich drawn barroom napkins, or perhaps thinking up policy during turbulence on The Lolita Express. Before them, we had an expanding middle class and increasing benefits for workers. President Richard Nixon created the Environmental Protection Agency and in 1974 offered Democratic legislative leader, Teddy Kennedy, a universal healthcare plan actually to the left of Obamacare. (Unions pressured Kennedy to hold out for a Democratic President to pass single payer. Bad call. Really bad call). So what the hell does all of this have to do with Michael Wolff being exposed by the Epstein emails not as savvy chronicler but sleazy advisor? Oh, we're getting there. And the billionaires who form the core of The Epstein List, and any other cataloguing of predatory activities, from private equity vulture capitalism to tech bro anti-vax vampirism. I give you two words, my friends: Two. Ok, three words, two phrases. Reagan. Human nature. I'll come back to both: | | ---|---|--- Psst: God isnot who entered the classroom Ya see, I went to a high school in New York City. The Horace Mann School to be exact, in the late 80s/early 90s. We would eventually be made aware--twenty-odd years later--of a pedophilia scandal that occurred right under our noses. No biggie, just the Headmaster (don't even think it) and President, R. Inslee Clark, who recruited me after 8th grade for my prowess on a dirt (and new-ish, high-falutin' polyurethane) track and as a right-winger (don't even think it) on the soccer pitch. To quote Forrest Gump, "Now you wouldn't believe me if I told you, but I could run like the wind blows ( don't even think...ok, enough). Clark also taught a fascinating class called "The Kennedy Years," during which he'd sometimes would walk up to the boys--almost always boys--and massage their shoulders during class for a minute or two before moving on. Meanwhile, my Music History teacher, Johannes Somary, would take classes of students on trips to Europe to see orchestras and opera. And to rape them. Thank God Guns n ' Roses and Aerosmith were more of my jam. These two pedophiles and others--a ring you could say--would begin to be exposed after suicides and lawsuits in 2012, and Horace Mann's reaction, ever the cloistered community for our masters of the universe, would at first downplay it, then hire "their own investigator" to look into it. Kinda like how OJ was gonna find the "real killers." That, my friends, is right around when I cut ties with the school. Forever. | | ---|---|--- There's still a Facebook page up called "Processing Horace Mann," set up by alums in the aftermath of stories breaking, for all of us to discuss the horrors committed by the predators at this elite institution, usually preying on those from poorer neighborhoods who were already made to feel out of place among kids who drove red BMW convertibles to school they got as a 17th birthday present (youngest you could drive alone in NYC), crashed within a week, only to get a brand new one (true story). In other words, those who needed friends and self esteem. And when this was all taking place? Clark was at Horace Mann from 1970-91, or during the time one of Horace Mann's league rivals, Dalton, employed a certain Jeffrey Epstein to teach math. Epstein sucked at it, and was fired. So, quite naturally, he ended up in the world of high finance (after rejecting an entreaty to join the NY Times--seriously, this man was a spy. The only other explanation is an ability to use the Jedi Mind trick on the unsuspecting). | | ---|---|--- Schools like Horace Mann and Dalton were in a league together to compete in athletics. So naturally we called ourselves the "Ivy League," which obviously wasn't the slightest bit pretentious. Just two weeks ago Jan Ransom of The NY Times made it clear Epstein had his hooks even further into these schools, as The Trinity School and Riverdale Country Day, both posh schools also catering to New York/North Jersey's elite, had "dozens of mentions" in the Epstein Files (also the Master's School in Westchester, NY, not in the "Ivy League." Oh how the must have suffered from that snub). In some cases, hopeful parents contacted Mr. Epstein for help with tuition or gaining admission for their children. In others, he appeared to reach out to the parents on his own initiative. Horace Mann has had a who's who of the elite attend over the years. Former New York Governor Elliot Spitzer (who had his own unrelated sex scandal that chased him from office), Arthur Hays Sulzberger, whose grandson A.G. turned The Times into the Biden Is Old Gazette because he was reportedly miffed at Biden for not doing sit down interviews with his paper. Maybe he should ask family members of Alex Pretti or soldiers on the ground in Iran if that was a responsible reaction to a one-sided dick measuring contest when his paper has an outsized influence on our democracy. And then there's James Murdoch (yes, that one). He was there when I was, the year behind me, both running the plush, dog-poop-filled fields of Van Cortlandt Park after school as members of the HM track team. James seemed like a nice enough kid at the time. His dad hadn't reached infamy yet, and I ended up at parties at his house now and again. He wasn't what you'd call an able runner, but he did need extra-curriculars and the track team didn't cut. And he got into Harvard, so I guess it worked. So you could say I had a front row seat--even though I didn't know it at the time--to how it would all fall apart as the spoiled, selfish self-aggrandizing elites of New York from the Trumps to the Lutnicks. There were many more names you'd know who were there, who've gone on to help corporatize media, criminalize key vectors of our economy, making millions of lives more miserable [This seems like a good time to mention I 'll be doing a 4-part, sit-down series where I will get deeply into the details of who I encountered and what I saw with Blue Amp Media Contributing Editor, Ellie Leonard]. But it's time for us to finally get to Michael Wolff's role in all this. As I said earlier, all it took was Reagan and human nature. Reagan, to detonate the New Deal consensus that for a half century had created the culture that sustained us and grew the largest middle class in the history of the world, making it possible for the existence of Jeffrey Epstein, Elon Musk, Donald Trump, and yes, pretend journalists like Michael Wolff. In the same way we talk about Trump destroying various guardrails today, the guardrails from the early 1930s to the late 1970s was the New Deal Consensus. Even a personally amoral man such as Nixon, as I described in the beginning of this piece, operated within it. Hell, Reagan, himself wasn't fully free of it, as he created The Veterans' Administration and issues a largescale amnesty for immigrants here illegally, Yet, Reagan unleashed that one force that has never left us throughout human history, which the New Deal had tamed, at least for a while. Th all-powerful, ancient and evil spirit of personal greed, which had only been held in check by legislation, and a popular culture that shamed anyone to openly displaying it since that fateful day the stock market crashed in of 1929. But once unshackled by The Gipper, it spread like a plague, dancing in the minds of men (and, to a far lesser degree, women), subsuming every institution it touched Greed took a hammer to the Overton Window. Gone was the worry one would achieve pariah status by proudly flying their greed-freak flag. Hobbes on Line 1! The state of nature, Line 2. Social acceptance of extreme wealth hoarding and ostentatious displays in not-very-long led to an outright celebration of it, it came to be seen as heroism. Movies of the time saw it coming, from corporate media (Network), to corporate Democrats (The Candidate) to unleashed corporate greed (Wall Street, New Jack City, Pretty Woman). The inevitable happened with the guardrails removed, as the accruing of obscene wealth and power, ludicrous CEO pay, stock manipulation, and gilded-age monopoly enveloped us. And the more we unshackled our psychopaths, sadists and narcissists who had felt their status--their general being--should be rewarded by collecting possessions, people, and wealth via exploitation and extraction, the more strove to control. There would never be enough. If you didn't know any of this, you might believe Michael Wolff was a reporter just trying to get to the bottom of the story of Jeffrey Epstein. What a crock of shit. | | ---|---|--- Wolff was never merely a reporter orbiting Jeffrey Epstein. He was a creature of this very ecosystem that made Epstein possible: the velvet-rope culture of New York ambition, where access was mistaken for intelligence, cruelty for sophistication, and proximity to predators was proof you mattered. He went to Montclair Kimberley, whom Horace Mann played in sports, and was like Horace Mann for the Northern Jersey folk. Then went to Vassar before transferring to Columbia University (where I went to grad school). Wolff wrote a book...about his own failure during the dot com bubble. Yes, a journalist trying to make it big on the interwebs so he could be in that big club! A columnist for New York Magazine , whose first instinct the moment it went up for sale wasn't to be concerned about editorial direction, his column, additional writing opportunities...but putting together the most gross group of marauders outside of Alien Vs Predator: Requiem to try and acquire it: Jeffrey Epstein, Harvey Weinstein, and Mort Zuckerman (an Epstein client who signed that infamous 50th birthday book, where Trump was...Trump) | | ---|---|--- Wherever was their other pal Wolff and Epstein's other pal they liked to spend time with, Woody Allen? Did he not have the funds to invest? Again, Wolff wanted to be The Story. Be in the big club. Remember James Murdoch, my schoolmate? Wolff wrote a book about dad, Rupert, who as much as any human being alive has preyed on the carcass of news media and American democracy with Fox "News," and his other vomitous mass of press outlets. So you'd think such an avatar of journalism done right, like Wolff, wouldn't defend Murdoch in his News International phone hacking scandal. You'd be wrong. Because Wolff wrote the book not to expose Murdoch, but to get to know him, become a power player, travel in his circles. As Michelle Cottle said of Wolff in a 2004 The New Republi c piece, he couldn't care less about the press. He's into: ...the power players--the moguls...fixated on culture, style, buzz, and money, money, money... So the newly revealed emails and back channeling didn't expose some shocking contradiction in Wolff's character. They exposed the character itself. Men like Wolff never believed their job was to challenge power. Their job was to flatter it just enough to stay invited to dinner, to the townhouse, to the after-party, to the whispered room where reputations were traded like stock options. | | ---|---|--- That is what people still miss about Epstein. He was not simply a singular monster. He was the logical endpoint of a culture that taught generations of elite men that appetite was genius and consequence was for other people --and then removed all barriers to their living out their twisted fantasies. Wolff, Murdoch, Trump, and their fellow social climbers didn't just tolerate this culture--they translated it into media, politics, and mythology. They made depravity look glamorous, corruption look inevitable, and exploitation look like the spoils of winning. To give you the whole George Calin quote as an apt summary for these men who now run politics, business, the military, and so much more, "they want your fucking retirement money, they want it back. So they can give it to their criminal friends on Wall Street. And you know something, they'll get it. They'll get it all from you sooner or later. 'Cause they own this fucking place. It's a big club... and you ain 't in it." Here's the part Democrats--and frankly the entire political media class--still haven't fully learned: This culture didn't disappear when Epstein died. It metastasized. James Murdoch was always in the big club. Michael Wolff sought to get in by any means necessary. I could never live with myself and be in it, so I walked away from it. And I've never regretted it. The same elite code remains: money as morality, access as virtue, cruelty as sophistication, and journalists too eager to turn monsters into mythology because proximity feels like power. That's why this fight is bigger than one dead predator or one grotesque social climber who made a career narrating the rot. I know, I've seen it, and I'll have much more to say about it going forward. Because this is about whether we finally build an independent media ecosystem strong enough to expose the entire predator class pipeline --from Reagan's worship of greed to Manhattan's salons to today's billionaire-authoritarian protection racket. That 's what we do here. Not just headlines. Not just outrage. A sustained, sharp, historically grounded case against the corruption culture that keeps manufacturing these men. This is not good.
The momentum behind our campaign has been _incredible._
**But right now, we have a problem – and I need your help.**
With our first FEC deadline of the year less than 8 hours away, we’re falling short of our critical $500,000 goal. **[Will you chip in $5 or more, split between our campaign and Chris Pappas, now to help us get back on track and show the sheer power of our grassroots movement?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260331_2.np8F67&refcode=em20260331-2&t=1&akid=5882%2E582294%2E9e3TXo)**
Let me explain why this goal is so important.
As I write this, my Republican opponent and his special interest allies are going all in to defeat me. They’re gearing up to pour millions into this race – and attack ads smearing my record have already started. It’s just a taste of what’s to come.
Their efforts prove one thing and one thing only: They are terrified of our message and our movement.
Our fight for working people is _popular._
Their fight for more profit off the backs of working people is not.
**But here’s the deal: They already have a massive war chest at their disposal – and the only way we’ll be able to compete is with unprecedented grassroots support from folks like you at crucial moments like this.**
**[So please, will you split $5 or more to help us raise the $500,000 we need before our first FEC deadline of 2026? Thank you so much,

body:
If you've ever planted a garden, you know it's not as simple as sticking a seed in the ground and hoping for the best.

| Peter, I love spring.

After months of gray skies and cold days, the world starts to come back to life; trees turn green, fields stretch out in color, and the sun finally sticks around long enough for us to enjoy it. Or at least... that's the dream. Iowa weather has been all over the place, but I'm manifesting those consistently warm, sunny days any minute now.

Spring always reminds me of what it takes to grow something meaningful.

If you've ever planted a garden, you know it's not as simple as sticking a seed in the ground and hoping for the best. You have to give it the right foundation, make sure the soil is healthy, water it consistently, and trust that with care and attention, it will grow into something beautiful.

That's exactly what this campaign has been like. Last year, we planted the seeds of this movement, and now, it's incredible to see how much our campaign is blooming. As I've traveled across the district, talking with Iowans from every corner and every background, I can feel the momentum building. People are ready for something better, and they're ready to fight for it.

But just like any garden, we need to keep putting in the work. We have to keep showing up, keep reaching people, and keep building the kind of campaign that can go the distance. That's why hitting our $30,000 end-of-quarter goal is so important right now – it's what allows us to turn this momentum into a victory in November.

If you can, I'd be so grateful if you donated today to help us close the gap toward our goal. # Juan Ciscomani is Funding Chaos, Not Security
---
| | In case you missed it, Jo wrote an op-ed in the Arizona Daily Star highlighting her support for law enforcement and public safety.
---
[|
---](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=faa8d6d170&e=fea3203902)
[|
---](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=c281bd1a61&e=fea3203902)
| | Read the highlights of the op-ed below, and the full piece [**HERE**](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=35f82f4cc8&e=fea3203902).
_"**I believe in the rule of law. I believe in public safety. And I believe that the men and women who enforce our laws deserve clear rules, serious training, and accountable leadership.** After 20 years of military service in the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps, several combat deployments and long days molding the next generation of leaders as a Drill Instructor at Quantico, I learned the lesson that still guides me today: Authority without discipline is dangerous, and force without accountability does not create security.”_
[...]
_“Southern Arizonans know how important it is to secure the border and protect public safety.**Organized criminal enterprises that smuggle fentanyl, narcotics, and people across the border must be stopped. We depend on the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to enforce the law, secure the border, and preserve public trust.** We also need lawful trade and travel, and an immigration system that works.”_
[...]
_“ True security doesn’t come from writing a blank check to a leaderless agency. That’s why I was outraged when our current Congressman, Juan Ciscomani, voted last year via the One Big Beautiful Bill Act to hand DHS a $150 billion slush fund designed to evade congressional oversight – **paid for by gutting Arizonans’ health care**.”_
---
| [Read the full op-ed here!](https://joannamendoza.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a848c5089d2c16d92422d70c8&id=0ade3aa095&e=fea3203902)

# No Kings Day
---

Fellow Conservative,

I said it earlier this week, and summarizes what Democrats have been up to the last 40+ days:

_“TSA agents are not getting paid, and they are showing up to work.

Democrats are getting paid, and they are not showing up for work.”_

Hardworking TSA officers secured our airports without paychecks for weeks , while Senate Democrats collected their six-figure salaries and skipped critical work — all to make a political statement.

Republicans have repeatedly voted to fully fund the Department of Homeland Security and ensure these essential workers get paid. Democrats blocked those efforts, choosing partisan games over the American people they were elected to serve.

This is exactly the kind of Washington dysfunction we’re fighting against in the Senate.

**[We now have just hours until the March 31st Q1 FEC deadline at midnight.](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=2ba20d2322704910ab1575cd8758f6d1&_e=CM-o8gufmbdBTeLQQTUvHzc8piw6i45dxWZLoXn226FEa2sO_e93AL8dnxcFAtSCkI4XP7iuA3U9NYfI5LGqrJQB_K_C6kCxhHXsUD1dF-G1toCjKnWJD542oPJqAc7AIUehFFVYrtrFSEzt7S31NoYJmQxrMcpEnNkBYc_yGR8P5gEhgp7MQm0_uCom1CmjsKZhVN_vfP6A88vehHouEnh2jeZcbypG3PuUP1LLTgUkDJf2y9G-7wjBgeawoaJAL5sghsr-N-92Z0T4ZEoTwdeStQPZitUNmavz13SSFqCZC8BviU3ZkkiaaGnlP-Q4DYSUyPgaOcU40hgPHNc4VTp7132HHlQDCYbAEnvkKMZxGcEvB1R46Po-GZ6kbwPymAmdR-gwu2CG94Ul-ALu9az240bEzjxOZMOWNlcJiGZCMFL_FCHs97KN-2kb_MTbZjRrrElop3y6Yrnf25aDRrsXyekKk7VB3rxxNbf5h7niQ6f6BZLhIMxb5kdPufR_UL0-rmsWorA7H4NTisGOg4p7hJuU3BDEcc6_ul7rutQfHGqYCyfY3HUe_gFJOdF6tKvQ2Vrpfdtf6hk0RCW1W7r8S3oDReJFA9mytlXAaXbibuNg_2hv6lA4SDLMK9uO6naRUj3aB8Kk-W3Xgw-JNMO0avyvoGPokxjI3q2nVNi_tMcy3gwWkJA1DEG0wcNrWnQkf7s6qI6LwwTYST0SGg%3D%3D)** I’m working every day to protect our Republican Senate majority and stop the radical left from regaining control. | | It’s no secret that House Republicans are in**panic mode.**
* They haven’t flipped a single seat anywhere in the country since Donald Trump returned to power, while Democrats have flipped more than two dozen.
* They know their paper-thin majority in Congress depends on defending toss-up districts like VA-02, but Virginia voters ushered in a blue wave last November.

subject: Broken promises
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Rosen for Nevada Rosen for Nevada
body:
| | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128497467/611495891/274859036?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5735-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNTRiOThiOC00ZDJkLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Pip7JJccgOYOLSddHShjWRhhoj2XQ4Nc3PHfsu_K5Ew=)
See, I get why some folks voted for Trump.
He promised to attack a broken system. And it’s a ripe target.
Even before Trump came on the scene, America had one of the most corrupt political systems in the Western world.
It’s been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money.
And it’s worse than ever now.
Citizens United was the worst court decision in modern American history.
When Members of Congress aren’t begging for money from Washington lobbyists, they’re trying to dodge getting carpet-bombed by super PACs.
Senators get threatened with millions of dollars of attack ads over the votes they take.
And see, that is why things don’t work for ordinary people.
It’s because the people’s elected representatives don’t represent the people. They represent the big donors!
That corruption is why they defunded nursing homes to cut taxes for the rich.
Corruption is why you pay a fortune for prescriptions.
Corruption is why your insurance claim keeps getting denied.
Corruption is why hedge funds get to buy up all the houses in your neighborhood, and then your corporate landlord ignores your calls during a gas leak.
Corruption is why that ambulance costs $3,000 after you just had to get your choking toddler to the hospital.
Yes, the system really is rigged.
But Trump’s not unrigging it. He’s re-rigging it for himself!
He’s a crook and a con man, and he wants to be a king.
You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund their hospitals and nursing homes.
You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund school lunch programs to help feed little boys and little girls whose hard-working parents are struggling to fill the fridge.
You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you do these things so you can cut taxes for the richest people in the country while you and your family business rake in massive sums from around the world.
Donald Trump’s second term has already done unfathomable damage to our country and the lives of millions of people.
And the people are beginning to see it.
But only by regaining Congressional power can we stop him.
Really.
The upcoming 2026 midterms are our last chance to restore checks and balances.
And my Senate race in Georgia is the single most critical contest: I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in 2026 in a state Trump carried in 2024.
**So if you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight for the future of this Republic –– please don’t wait until 2028:_[Split a donation of $5 between Jacky Rosen and my reelection campaign in Georgia right now.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128497468/611495904/274859036?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&refcode=jtk5735-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNTRiOThiOC00ZDJkLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Pip7JJccgOYOLSddHShjWRhhoj2XQ4Nc3PHfsu_K5Ew=)_**

[Joe Nocera](https://substack.com/redirect/3ab09d44-4ded-4de9-9388-facf61f584a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s compelling article in *The Free Press* tackles one of the most uncomfortable questions facing modern academia: the extent to which scientific research is fraudulent, fabricated, or fundamentally compromised. Published on March 10, 2026, "[How Much of Science Is Fake?"](https://substack.com/redirect/d0501b60-bd37-4680-9913-e51d7a69e716?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) pulls back the curtain on a crisis that threatens the foundations of human knowledge.

For decades, scientists enjoyed a position of near-unassailable authority in public discourse. As Nocera observes, scientists "were above reproach." Yet mounting evidence suggests that trust may have been misplaced. The article explores what happens when the scientific method itself becomes corrupted by incentives that prioritize publication volume over rigorous truth-seeking.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.tI4YvLr_uQ6ncCLnt6P3iCtpmQgota7hAfkb0y3cxGg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=192786735)
Central to Nocera's investigation is a new class of researcher: the fraud hunter. These independent sleuths--including microbiologist Elisabeth Bik and psychologist Brian Nosek of the Center for Open Science--have dedicated themselves to exposing image manipulation, statistical irregularities, and outright fabrication in peer-reviewed papers. Their work has revealed systemic vulnerabilities in scientific publishing that allow fraudulent research to proliferate unchecked.

The scope of the problem is staggering. Citing work from researchers like Stuart Ritchie, author of *Science Fictions: Exposing Fraud, Bias, Negligence and Hype in Science*, Nocera documents how "p-hacking" (manipulating data to achieve statistical significance), publication bias, and outright fabrication have become endemic in certain fields. The reproducibility crisis--where studies cannot be replicated when repeated by independent researchers--represents merely the visible tip of a much darker iceberg. Nosek's landmark work demonstrated that a significant percentage of published findings in psychology failed to replicate, shaking confidence in decades of research.

Behind the statistics lie human costs: patients receiving treatments based on fraudulent clinical trials, policymakers crafting regulations on fabricated environmental data, and genuine scientists seeing their fields discredited by bad actors. The article highlights how predatory journals, pay-to-publish models, and the relentless pressure to "publish or perish" create perfect conditions for misconduct to flourish.

Yet Nocera does not present a counsel of despair. Instead, he profiles the reformers working to restore scientific integrity. Open-science movements advocating for data sharing, preregistered studies, and transparent peer review offer pathways toward accountability. Technology is helping too: AI-powered tools can now detect manipulated images, while platforms like PubPeer enable post-publication scrutiny.

The article concludes that science's salvation may lie in its own self-correcting nature--but only if the scientific community embraces radical transparency. Nocera argues for fundamental reforms: better funding for replication studies, harsher penalties for misconduct, and a cultural shift away from valuing quantity over quality in research output.

Ultimately, Nocera's piece serves as both a warning and a call to action. Science remains humanity's most powerful tool for understanding reality, but its credibility is a finite resource. Without meaningful intervention to root out fraud and restore public confidence, science risks becoming just another institution whose authority cannot be trusted. The question posed in the headline is provocative, but the answer Nocera provides is nuanced: not *all* science is fake--far from it--but the systems designed to ensure integrity have failed spectacularly, and fixing them is an urgent necessity for the future of human knowledge.

This is how they test our democracy:
First, it’s a letter.
Then it’s a threat.
Then it’s voter data demanded under pressure.
That’s exactly what Pam Bondi tried in Minnesota — and it won’t stop there unless other states push back now .
Tonight at midnight is our first end-of-quarter fundraising deadline of 2026. And this deadline matters because it’s not just about dollars — it’s about momentum. Please make a campaign donation before the deadline. We’re still about $2,150 shy of our goal – and I’m counting on you. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260331em]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260331em]
Trump and his allies are looking for new ways to get at voter rolls, intimidate states, and undermine trust in elections. They’re testing who will fold — and who will fight.
In Oregon, we choose to fight.
We’ve set a clear goal: raise $5,000 by midnight tonight to show that Oregonians are united, organized, and ready to defend our democracy before it’s under siege here.
If you’ve been waiting to step in, this is the moment. A contribution in these final hours helps us stay on offense — protecting voters and ensuring no one bullies our state into surrendering its election infrastructure.
This is our first major test of 2026. Let’s send a message that Oregon won’t be intimidated.
Please chip in before midnight and help us close January strong. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260331em]
Thank you,

After the 2026 elections are over, we might be able to look back on this past week as a glaring warning of what was to come.
In what Donald Trump’s former Chief Strategist Steve Bannon suggests could be a “test run” for the midterms, Trump has deployed ICE agents to airports — where his refusal to fund the TSA has led to severe screening delays, with lines stretching out the door.
**Bannon already said “we’re gonna have ICE surround the polls come November.”** Now we see Trump using this paramilitary force in the middle of his funding standoff with Democrats in Congress, who insist upon basic accountability measures for ICE agents.
Of course, ICE doesn’t have any business in monitoring polling places. And the federal government does not have the authority to manage elections.

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: One last, humble request
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
The Secretary of Defense just tried to cash-in on the sacrifice of the men and women he leads. It’s so staggeringly corrupt that it is hard to wrap your head around.
#

Peter, we’ve got just a few hours until our quarterly FEC deadline at midnight tonight.
That deadline comes at a moment unlike any other in our nation’s history.
I served in Iraq as a Marine at the height of the war, about 20 years ago. After I came home, one of my greatest fears was that another generation of kids would have to go through what I did. But I never would’ve guessed the president himself would be this grave a threat to our democracy. I signed up to defend our Constitution, but I didn’t think I’d have to do it at home.
This is authoritarianism. It is here. The president is personally starting his own wars, and the GOP is doing nothing to stop it. We need to stand up now or risk losing the rights and liberties we were born with.
You know what’s happening, but most people are only just waking up to that reality. If we’re going to build a movement that stops and reverses Trump’s power grab, we have to start reaching the people who aren’t reading the news every day.
That’s why I’m trying to meet and speak to people beyond just cable news. It’s why I’m doing podcasts and social media, interviews with local and national papers. It’s why I’m doing town halls and traveling to battleground states to support candidates in tough races.
That’s what I did in my campaign. It’s what I’ve been doing since I got elected. And I’m going to keep doing it as long as I have to until we start to break through to people.

This may be uncomfortable to hear.
But most political donations don’t change who wins elections.
They fund activity, not outcomes.
They pay for:
* TV ads that voters ignore
* Consultants who write memos
* Events that make insiders feel important

Meanwhile, elections are decided by something much more basic:
**➡️ Which side puts more paper in the ballot box.**
Charlie Kirk understood this before anyone.
In 2024, he deployed THOUSANDS of ballot-chasers to find and engage voters who hadn’t participated in recent elections.
His teams would follow up, visit, call, text...**__they did whatever it took__** to ensure voters banked their votes before Election Day.
He jokingly called his ballot-chasing operation “polite nagging.”
**Well, Charlie’s polite nagging won _big_.**
Republicans didn’t just win – they _swept_ – and Charlie’s ballot-chasing army delivered all 5 swing states for President Trump.
**[Now, we’re digging in ahead of Midterms and the Democrat’s billion dollar ground effort is already in overdrive. Will you stand with us right now?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e15240562/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZtY19oYXRyLXBvZG8tZHJzX2JyXzIwMjYwMzMxLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAzMzE/LbmNsbXBCU2FLcQ/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9MDMyMGVtNyZ1dG1fdGVybT0yMjczM193cjE/gacxJVg/s2p79c28c46)**
Turning Point PAC is funding a hiring surge: **700 _new_ full-time ballot-chasers** to join teams already deployed in key districts.
Each ballot-chaser has a clear operational target:
➡️ Find and identify voters and commit to banking **10 ballots a day** in the early voting periods
For this new class of 700 chasers, that adds up to:
* 7,000 votes per day
* 140,000+ votes in 20 days

**Those margins decide Congress.**
Don’t waste another dollar on strategies that feel good but don’t produce wins.
Fund logistics. Fund turnout. Fund ballot-chasing.
🟢 $50 → Sponsors **1 ballot-chaser** 🟢 $100 → Sponsors **2 ballot-chasers** 🟢 $250 → Powers a **targeted turnout team** 🟢 $500 → Funds a **major precinct push** 🟢 $1,000+ → **Maximum impact**
Invest in what works.

For Charlie, ****

body:
| | | Hi there, it's Mark Kelly, senator for Arizona and Vice Chair of the DSCC. I'm going to ask you to [**contribute to our mission to flip the Senate blue,**](https://go.dscc.org/go/22350?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20260331-MarkKelly-KellyWouldntAskFR-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20260331-MarkKelly-KellyWouldntAskFR-Pros-sl1&akid=23286%2E9716520%2EK3j4WF) but before I do, let me explain why:

I know a thing or two about tough Senate races because I won two back‐to‐back battleground races to serve Arizona today.

First in 2020, I flipped Arizona's seat blue in a special election — one of the hardest, closest races in the country.

Then in 2022, I had to do it all over again — but this time, my team and I more than doubled our margin of victory.

**Now, I'm proud to be leading the fight to take back the Senate in 2026, because strong campaigns make a difference, and every race requires hard work, focus, and resources.**

Peter,
A little over a week ago, we pushed our team to set an ambitious goal to close this fundraising quarter.
This is not some arbitrary goal. As we write this, our lawyers are engaged in a legal battle that is life or death for the Colorado redistricting effort. On trial is whether MAGA can introduce a dueling redistricting ballot measure aimed at confusing voters and gumming up the works.
Our lawyers need more firepower and since we announced our goal, we've seen an unprecedented surge of support.
People from across the country--from Colorado, Ohio, Alabama, Montana, New York, and literally every other state--have chipped in and left notes about how fired up they are. How ready they are to fight back. How tired they are of watching Republicans rig the maps while Democrats play nice.
But as we get closer to midnight donations have slowed. And we are cutting it close.
Right now our team is white knuckling it. We're only $421 away from hitting our goal--but we haven't received a donation in over 15 minutes and midnight is a little over an hour away.
If just 20 supporters chipped in $20 right now, we'd have the resources we need to fight back against MAGA's election rigging and put our initiative on the ballot.

**Redistricting Crisis: State of the States**
**Virginia:** On April 21, Virginians will vote in a special election to determine whether the state will redraw its maps to counter Republican power grabs across the country. **Missouri:** Voters are fighting back after an extreme gerrymander by Republicans — mobilizing to force a statewide vote in November on the new map and taking a case all the way up to the Missouri Supreme Court. **Florida:** Florida recently passed an extreme voter identification law — its own version of the SAVE Act — and Gov. Ron DeSantis has called for a special legislative session to enact a mid-decade redraw to create a congressional map that would further diminish the voting power of communities of color. **Utah:** With support from Donald Trump, Republicans tried to repeal a law that created the state’s bipartisan map commission, now that a new, fairer map indicates that a Democrat might be able to win a congressional seat. Voters recently were able to stop this effort from moving forward, but we are waiting to see what Republicans will try next! **Wisconsin:** On April 7, Wisconsin will elect a new state supreme court justice in a critical race that will have a lasting impact on fair representation in this critical battleground state. **Louisiana:** The U.S. Supreme Court is currently considering _Louisiana v. Callais_ , a case that will determine the future of the Voting Rights Act and could lead to the loss of congressional seats across the U.S. South — further diluting the power of minority voters nationwide. Some state legislators are already proposing new versions of the congressional map to implement this change!

clean_body: Donate to help win key battles for fair representation | Peter, America’s redistricting crisis has been building for decades — and this year it’s reached unprecedented levels of anti-democratic, power-hungry madness. Today, as we wrap up one of the last fundraising quarters before the midterm elections, we’re providing a lightning round of updates from key redistricting battles nationwide. You can skip ahead to the updates = | = Redistricting Crisis: State of the States Virginia: On April 21, Virginians will vote in a special election to determine whether the state will redraw its maps to counter Republican power grabs across the country. Missouri: Voters are fighting back after an extreme gerrymander by Republicans — mobilizing to force a statewide vote in November on the new map and taking a case all the way up to the Missouri Supreme Court. Florida: Florida recently passed an extreme voter identification law — its own version of the SAVE Act — and Gov. Ron DeSantis has called for a special legislative session to enact a mid-decade redraw to create a congressional map that would further diminish the voting power of communities of color. Utah: With support from Donald Trump, Republicans tried to repeal a law that created the state’s bipartisan map commission, now that a new, fairer map indicates that a Democrat might be able to win a congressional seat. Voters recently were able to stop this effort from moving forward, but we are waiting to see what Republicans will try next! Wisconsin: On April 7, Wisconsin will elect a new state supreme court justice in a critical race that will have a lasting impact on fair representation in this critical battleground state. Louisiana: The U.S. Supreme Court is currently considering Louisiana v. Callais , a case that will determine the future of the Voting Rights Act and could lead to the loss of congressional seats across the U.S. South — further diluting the power of minority voters nationwide. Some state legislators are already proposing new versions of the congressional map to implement this change! Peter, there’s no time to waste. The attacks on fair representation are relentless — and we must be relentless, too. = We’ll have more updates from these key battlegrounds in the days and weeks ahead. [1]Justice Democrats

In case you missed it,
Peter, we just endorsed
progressive candidates in two more Democratic primary races: Saikat
Chakrabarti in CA-11 and Dr. Adam Hamawy in NJ-12.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260331-2.qu3wGy&refcode=em20260331-37627&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37627%2E1203867%2E9jQEw5 ]Tweet from Drop Site discussing Justice Democrats' endorsement of
Saikat Chakrabarti and Dr. Adam Hamawy

These primaries are just over two months away, and both are big
opportunities to send pro-peace, anti-corporate champions for the working
class to join our bloc in Congress.

But before we get there, we’re hours away from our critical end-of-quarter
fundraising deadline at midnight tonight.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260331-2.qu3wGy&refcode=em20260331-37627&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37627%2E1203867%2E9jQEw5 ]Can you rush $5 or more right now to help us power these
campaigns and build the grassroots momentum it will take to win?

In former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi’s district, we have the rare chance
to replace a seat controlled by Democratic leadership with Saikat, a bold
progressive who co-founded Justice Democrats and is ready to keep fighting
for the people’s agenda in Washington.

In New Jersey, we can elect Dr. Hamawy: a veteran who’s staunchly against
more forever wars, and a doctor who has saved lives during the genocide in
Gaza while supporting Medicare for All here at home.

Both of these races are open primaries. Both are happening in just over
two months. And both represent a real chance to elect a new generation of
unbought leadership to Congress.

But we can’t do it without the grassroots resources to compete against
AIPAC, the Big Tech super PACs, and their right-wing billionaire donors.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260331-2.qu3wGy&refcode=em20260331-37627&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=37627%2E1203867%2E9jQEw5 ]Chip in whatever you can to ensure we hit our $50,000 end-of-quarter
goal before midnight. Your contribution will directly fuel our fight to
elect Saikat, Dr. Hamawy, and the rest of our 2026 slate!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260331-2.qu3wGy&refcode=em20260331-37627&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=37627%2E1203867%2E9jQEw5 ]Contribute $5

Every dollar helps us organize earlier, reach more voters, and take on the
full weight of the Democratic establishment and its corporate backers. If
we’re going to meet the urgency of this moment, it starts with what we do
now.

— Justice Democrats

Robinson Report subscribers are familiar with the MaineCare fraud reporting we've been pumping out, including the piece published March 19 on Paradise Residential Services LLC.
If you're only getting news from the taxpayer-subsidized Maine Public website, then you had to a full 12 days to get a rehashed, less detailed, less informative version of the story with no interviews and no named sources.
Here's taxpayer-funded journalism thief Patty Wight's inspiring take on a sensational story that I told nearly two weeks earlier:
> The state of Maine has terminated its contract with a Portland-based residential care provider for people with intellectual disabilities, citing health and safety violations.
> Maine's Department of Health and Human Services notified Paradise Residential Services in a letter on March 6 that it was terminating its MaineCare contract as of March 9 because clients were in "immediate jeopardy."
> The Department detailed multiple violations, including residents who were left unsupervised, inadequate food, and unsanitary conditions, including 'resident incontinence hidden in closets rather than properly cleaned.'
> A spokesperson for the Department says its Rapid Response Team is transitioning clients to new group homes, but declined to comment further due to an ongoing appeals process.
> Paradise Residential Services has also drawn scrutiny from the Trump administration and state Republican lawmakers following reports in conservative media outlets that it overbilled MaineCare for services.
First of all: The last paragraph is not accurate. There weren't "outlets" plural, there was _an_ outlet. This one. And Patty Whatshername almost certainly knows how to spell my name and link to the original report, which contained lengthy, on-the-record interviews with former employees, as well as a detailed explanation of the financial scheme Paradise Residential Services used to maximize the owners' personal income. This alleged journalist can't even name the proprietors of this particular business ventures -- and we all know why that is.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5ba7c286-cdbb-496a-9a0b-9ad07c6af052?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There was never a finding by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) that Paradise Residential Services "overbilled" Medicaid, aka MaineCare. That was the case with Gateway Community Services and Bright Future Healthier You, the two Somali-owned MaineCare businesses that have been raided by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security in recent months. But that was not the case with Paradise.
We know this because, unlike Maine Public, we file Freedom of Access Act requests to obtain information the government doesn't want public -- like the Notices of Violation that DHHS sends to MaineCare providers when audits catch them overbilling. In the documents we received, Paradise Residential Services was not listed. Although Paradise Residential Services has billed in the 75th percentile and even the 95 percentile for all providers of residential care services nationally, that's a finding original to our analysis and not something DHHS concluded. In other words, DHHS never caught them. DHHS is only taking action now that the Trump Administration has increased scrutiny of MaineCare.
The truth is that disabled Mainers are now being rescued from deplorable conditions because of Trump and the "conservative" media, yet Maine Public's [story](https://substack.com/redirect/1909c266-0d12-4015-88b8-571deaab290f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) makes us out to be antagonists, without even having the courage to name us.
Here's one story the sloths at Maine Public definitely won't steal...

---|---|---
Look at the latest Form 990 for Maine Public. In addition to the outrageously high and totally unearned salaries of the leftists running that operation, you'll notice that Tarlan Ahmadov is still on the board. That's the same Tarlan Ahamdov that was ousted for his roll as Gov. Janet Mills' Office of New Americans Director for his vile bigotry against Armenians.
What a nice operation they're running there -- on our dime.
